data.title: Designing for the Eye: Optical corrections in architecture and typography
data.author: ArmageddonIt
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了建筑和字体设计中的光学修正（或光学调整），强调视觉设计需考虑光学错觉。文章以Müller-Lyer错觉为例，说明两条等长线因箭头方向不同而看似长度不一，这种错觉不受文化背景限制，甚至在动物界也能观察到。作者提到，视觉艺术家、字体设计师等应依赖眼睛的判断，而非单纯依靠测量。文中引用了Paul Renner的《The Art of Typography》一书，指出对于艺术家而言，没有光学错觉，他们从一开始就考虑了表象形式，并根据视觉印象工作。最终，当视觉印象与测量冲突时，应优先考虑视觉印象。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：设计与美学在不同领域（科技、建筑、字体、音乐、logo设计等）中的体现和争议

不同观点：
• 关于微软设计的评价：
  - [1970-01-01] 认为微软以前的Windows和Office具有" brutalist beauty "，可以高度自定义，而如今的O365和Azure设计则像是对其 former design 的讽刺。
  - 反对观点隐含在[soperj]的评论中，指出微软的设计缺乏原创性，甚至抄袭了Xerox Parc和Braun的设计理念，批评其"没有品味"。

• 关于知识内化与技术依赖的讨论：
  - [anactofgod] 认为互联网和AI使得人们不再重视自身知识的积累，强调只有当知识内化于心时，才能产生新的见解。
  - 该观点未在其他评论中直接回应，但隐含了对技术进步（如AI）影响传统认知方式的质疑。

• 关于HDR和图像处理技术的讨论：
  - [Lu2025] 提出iPhone 16的HDR照片显得“overprocessed”和“cartoonish”，尽管技术上更接近人眼的动态范围，但视觉上感觉不自然。
  - 没有直接反对意见，但该评论指出了现代图像技术在追求真实感时可能带来的不适。

• 关于建筑与字体设计中的光学平衡：
  - [necovek] 强调现代建筑和字体设计忽视了光学平衡，认为这是美观的重要因素，并通过帕特农神庙柱子的设计为例说明。
  - 该观点未受到直接反驳，反而通过[bitwize]的评论得到了支持，后者通过LilyPond音乐排版中的不对称美化细节进一步论证了设计中的光学调整。

• 关于Taj Mahal设计的讨论：
  - [zeckalpha] 指出Taj Mahal并非方形设计，使其看起来像是正方形，这是一个未被提及但值得注意的设计细节。
  - 该评论未引发争议，只是作为一个补充的设计例子。

• 关于字体设计在HN上受欢迎程度的讨论：
  - [pcrh] 对字体设计在Hacker News上受欢迎表示好奇，认为其受欢迎程度高于其他设计形式。
  - 该观点未引发直接讨论，但隐含了对设计社区兴趣点的观察。

• 关于logo设计的实用建议：
  - [taneq] 提供了关于logo设计的建议，强调logo应尽量适应盒子形状，保持重心稳定，并避免不对称设计以免布局不协调。
  - 该观点未受到直接反驳，更多是作为实用设计技巧分享。

• 关于哥特式建筑与字体演化的讨论：
  - [hoseja] 解释了哥特式建筑与当时书写风格的演化关系，指出并非有意对应，而是工具和技术限制下的自然演化。
  - 该评论未引发直接争议，但提供了对历史设计演化的另一种解释。

补充讨论：
- 设计美学在不同领域（科技产品、建筑、字体、音乐等）中的共通性与差异性。
- 技术进步（如HDR、AI）对传统设计理念的冲击与适应。
- 设计中的光学平衡与不对称调整在不同设计领域中的重要性。
- 历史设计演化与现代设计理念的对比与反思。

争议焦点：
- 微软设计的评价与技术抄袭争议。
- 知识内化与技术依赖之间的平衡。
- 现代技术追求真实感与传统视觉审美之间的矛盾。

Designing for the Eye
Optical Corrections in Architecture and Typography
By Niko Kitsakis, June 2025
This article highlights a special aspect of both visual design and architecture: Optical cor­rections (or optical ad­just­ments, if you prefer). If you found
my piece about legible typefaces
interesting, youâll likely enjoy this one as well. Since I included many visual examples that are size-sensitive, make sure you read this on a big screen and not your mobile device.
Optical Illusions
The MÃ¼ller-Lyer illusion, pictured below, makes you think that, of two lines, one is longer than the other when in fact they are of the same length. It appears in virtually every introductory book on graphic de­sign and, of course, in books on per­ception and psy­cho­lo­gy. You might not have known it by name, but you must have seen it before:
â
â
Is the blue line on top longer than the one at the bottom? Click the arrows to find out.
It used to be said that, in order to see the illu­sion, you must have grown up in an environ­ment where lines very similar to these would explicitly appear in your everyday surroundings â in architecture and furniture, for example, or when you had played with building blocks as a kid and so on. This is, incidentally, what I too was taught at my school of visual design some decades ago. However, I always had a hard time be­liev­ing it, and according to
some new research
, this is indeed not the case: Not only can the illu­sion be per­ceived by anyone, no matter their cultural background, it even extends (to some degree) to the animal kingdom and can be ex­pe­ri­enced in a haptic version as well.
The reason why I never really believed that the MÃ¼ller-Lyer illusion (and others like it) would work only on people who grew up in our Western culture is that, in the first place, it seems visually far too uni­ver­sal to begin with. After all, theyâre just lines. You can draw them in the sand, and they can appear naturally in many circum­stan­ces. When I look at another person, my brain will assign certain values to the length of that personâs arms, legs, and torso, and memorise them as some variety of line as well. If the brain didnât do that, we would not be able to tell if a body or facial features were out of proportion. So in my view, something dis­cern­ible only by people from a specific culture would have to be far more elaborate than an optical illusion of just a few lines.
While that was only my personal gut-feeling, I soon dis­co­vered that other people had made similar obser­va­tions. One such time was when I first read Paul Rennerâs 1940 book
Die Kunst der Typo­grafie
(The Art of Typo­graphy). The book covers pretty much every­thing you need to know to become a typo­graph­er, in­clu­ding that you should not rely on mea­su­ring things but rather on what your own eyes tell you:
Der glaube an das ZÃ¤hlen und Messen verfÃ¼hrt in allen KÃ¼nsten zu den grÃ¶bsten Fehlern.
The belief in counting and measuring leads to the grossest errors in all the arts.
Renner happens to show the MÃ¼ller-Lyer illusion in his book and writes about what to make of it and other visual illusions like it. Take a look at this book spread first:
If you read books, you have an advantage.
If you look closely, you can see a version of the MÃ¼ller-Lyer illusion in the top right box of the left page. Renner describes every optical illu­sion on that page separately, but whatâs interesting is how he con­clu­des that section. He says that the following applies to all of the optical illusions:
FÃ¼r die Anschauungsweise des KÃ¼nstlers, des Schriftschneiders und des Typographen gibt es hier keine optischen TÃ¤uschungen, sie rechnen von vornherein mit den scheinbaren Formen; was scheinbar falsch ist, ist fÃ¼r sie falsch; und was scheinbar richtig ist, ist fÃ¼r sie richtig. Es handelt sich also nicht darum, ein genaues ZÃ¤hlen, Messen und Bauen durch ein unbestimmtes, schwankendes, willkÃ¼rliches GefÃ¼hl, das niemand nach­prÃ¼fen kann, zu ersetzen, sondern man soll einfach den wirklichen Augenschein, dessen Feststellung ein sehr geÃ¼btes Auge erfordert, als maÃgeblich anerkennen; er ist zwar âsubjektivâ, aber er ist, wie die Gelehrten sagen, âintersubjektiv gleichâ, also bei allen Menschen den gleichen TÃ¤uschungen unterworfen. Da alle bildende Kunst fÃ¼r den Augenschein arbeitet, so mÃ¼ssen wir ihm Ã¼berall dort recht geben, wo er mit der Zahl und der Messung in Widerspruch gerÃ¤t.
From the perspective of the artist, the punchcutter, and the typographer, there are no optical illusions here â they assume from the outset the apparent forms; what appears false is false for them, and what appears correct is correct for them. It is therefore not a matter of replacing precise counting, measuring, and constructing with a vague, fluctuating, arbitrary feeling that no one can verify, but rather of simply recognising the actual visual impression â whose assessment requires a very well-trained eye â as autho­ri

data.title: The Story of Mel, A Real Programmer, Annotated (1996)
data.author: fanf2
data.article_summary: 《The Story of Mel, A Real Programmer》是由Ed Nather撰写的经典故事，描述了一位名叫Mel的真正程序员，他通过巧妙的手工优化，在早期计算机上实现了高效的程序运行。Mel以其出色的编程技巧和对机器底层的深刻理解而闻名。Erik Brunvand为此故事做了注释，解释了其中的技术细节和历史背景，帮助现代读者理解早期计算机编程的挑战和魅力。这篇文章通过生动的叙述展现了早期计算机时代的编程文化和程序员的智慧。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕“LGP-30计算机”及其相关历史、技术细节、人物“Mel”的讨论

不同观点：
• **drfuchs** 提到LGP-30的详细手册可以在网上找到，并分享了自己在1973年学习LGP-30汇编语言的经历。他认为从底层机器语言学起有助于理解计算机的运行原理，但这种方法在今天不再普遍。
• **alnwlsn** 提到YouTuber David收到了LGP-21计算机以及一些LGP-30代码，其中包括Mel编写的程序。尽管Mel的代码比传闻中更清晰，但LGP-30的自修改代码是一个预期功能。他还提到目前没有找到太多关于LGP-21的文档，研究这些代码可能有助于理解LGP-21。
• **anyfoo** 提到一个关于Mel的播客，并建议在听之前先了解“The Story of Mel”这篇文章，以更好地理解播客内容。
• **naniwaduni** 分享了一个小知识点：LGP-30的十六进制数字使用的是非标准的“0-9fgjkqw”表示法。

补充讨论：
• **dang** 提到关于Mel的讨论在社区中时有出现，并列举了过去几年相关讨论的链接，显示出社区对Mel及LGP-30相关历史的持续兴趣。
• **ksenzee** 幽默地指出，1996年的注释中对“硬盘”和“软盘”的解释现在可能需要进一步注释。
• **oc1** 提到遇到过像Mel一样的程序员，他们拒绝适应新技术和AI工具，但自己却在快速发展并部署应用。
• **habedi0** 简单地问道“The Story of Mel”是否足够说明问题。
• **anteloper** 和 **reverendsteveii** 都表达了对“The Story of Mel”这篇文章的喜爱，前者称其为精彩的阅读，后者将其比作互联网时代的“申命记”。
• **BruceEel** 对LGP-30的“磁鼓记忆”是否存在照片表示好奇。
• **andybak** 幽默地评论说“要是有超链接就好了”，暗示早期文档缺乏现代的链接便利。

争议焦点：
• 关于从底层机器语言学起是否仍然是必要的教育方法存在不同看法。drfuchs认为这种方法对他有效，但现代不一定普遍适用。

总体来看，讨论围绕LGP-30和Mel的历史、技术细节、代码研究及其在计算机历史中的地位展开，参与者分享了个人经历、资源链接和对相关技术的兴趣。

data.title: My Family and the Flood
data.author: herbertl
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讲述了作者一家在德州瓜达卢佩河边度假时遭遇洪水袭击的经历。四岁的Rosemary最先醒来，告诉父亲Lance屋顶有异响。不久后，大家被雷雨惊醒，发现河水迅速上涨，已逼近他们建在桩上的房子甲板。洪水迅速逼近，最终冲破玻璃门涌入屋内。在混乱中，一家人忙着保护孩子并试图寻找逃生方法，但水位持续上升，房屋开始变形，情况十分危急。最终，他们在洪水中挣扎，等待可能的救援。

44576352.article_content:
Rosemary, the four-year-old, woke up first. She told my brother-in-law, Lance, that there was something on the roof.
Seven of us were at my family’s river house on the Guadalupe, between Ingram and Hunt, for the Fourth. Our little stretch of river is wide, green, cool, deep, and slow. It is some of the best swimming anywhere and one of the most beautiful spots in Texas, as far as I’m concerned. I’ve spent many peaceful afternoons there, floating and staring up at the cypress trees that tower over the water. The house, a one-story cabin on stilts about fifty yards from the river up our steeply sloped yard, was built right after the
1987 flood
that devastated this region, killing ten teenagers. Concrete pillars put our family’s place a few feet above what officials consider a one-hundred-year floodplain. More than once I’d tried to imagine the waters rising that high, but it seemed impossible.
We’d had pizza for dinner and spent that Thursday evening playing hide-and-seek with Rosemary, a rambunctious, expressive, willful little girl with blond hair and blue eyes who can speak Spanish and calls me Tío, and her baby brother, my twenty-month-old nephew, Clay, a towhead who’d just learned to say the words “boo” and “yellow.” After the kids went to sleep, a few of us played charades until about 9:30 p.m., when we all said goodnight and went to bed.
I woke around 3 a.m. to the sound of thunder and rain. My only thought was, I hope it stops so I can go on an early-morning run. Shortly before 4:30, I would later learn, Rosemary climbed down from the top bunk of the kids’ bedroom and went to get her father. Lance stepped out of bed to see what was causing all the pounding and creaking. I stirred at about that time, too, and heard what I figured were the kids running around the house, excited by the storm. Or maybe the winds were causing tree branches to slam against the metal roof. I heard Lance call out for his wife, my sister Alissa, and I got out of bed and walked into the main living area. I saw my dad, Clint, who is 73, and Lance peering out through the sliding-glass doors that led to the back deck. The house was dark, but Dad held a flashlight, aiming it into the night.
“What’s going on?” I asked.
“We’re in trouble,” he said. “Big trouble.”
I looked past them. The river was as high as the deck, twenty feet above the ground.
We had spent so many hours on that porch looking out over the yard and to the river below. Now the water splashed against the bottom of its railing. The gravity of our situation didn’t sink in right away, but the facts were clear: We were surrounded by fast-moving floodwater, and we had no way of escaping to higher ground.
Rosemary and Clay Parisher in Austin this summer.
Courtesy of Darhys Rodriguez
I ran back to my bedroom and woke up my husband, Patrick. Soon all of us—Dad, Lance, Alissa, Rosemary, Clay, Patrick, and me—came together in the living area. Clay flashed his adorable smirk at Patrick, eager to play. We talked through our options. Getting onto the roof was impossible. We had no ladder, and the eaves were about eight feet above the deck. Patrick weighed whether we could all climb through a window into the live oak whose branches were near the back of the house, then realized it wasn’t reachable. Lance called 911, but the dispatcher said he didn’t know when anyone could get to us.
I tried to imagine a scenario that would turn out okay. I imagined rescuers in a yellow raft emerging from the darkness. I imagined being stuck in the house for hours or days, grateful for all the groceries we’d brought for the weekend. I imagined my husband pointing out that the floodwaters were starting to recede. I imagined the relief I would feel when I realized he was right.
The river rose. Within a minute or two it was about a foot high against the glass door. We got dressed, put on shoes, and packed bags so we could be ready to leave in case someone, anyone, miraculously arrived.
The family river house, near Ingram, in 2021.
Courtesy of Aaron Parsley
As we reassembled in the kitchen, the vinyl flooring under our feet started to bubble, and then water began to pool. My dad walked into his bedroom and saw the carpet floating off the floor. The river’s musty scent permeated the house, mixed with what smelled like freshly chopped wood. My sister sat Rosemary and Clay on the kitchen island countertop. We discussed whether we could get them higher, maybe even on top of the cabinets in the small space below the ceiling. Then the roof over the porch crashed down and we heard glass shatter in my father’s room, just off the kitchen.
Rosemary asked, “Why did the window break?”
Clay started to cry.
When the sliding-glass door opened and water poured in, Lance ran to it, shoved it closed, and held it shut. The pendant lamps began to swing wildly over the kitchen counter. The house was shifting. data.title: Running a million-board chess MMO in a single process
data.author: isaiahwp
data.article_summary:
《Running a million-board chess MMO in a single process》一文介绍了名为"One Million Chessboards"的在线国际象棋游戏。该游戏由1000x1000的棋盘组成，棋子可以在不同棋盘间移动，所有玩家的动作是实时同步的，没有回合限制。游戏在一个单一进程中运行，作者通过使用Golang和Protobufs等技术，优化了性能，确保了客户端能快速响应。游戏初期吸引了超过15万玩家，产生了数百万次移动和查询。

游戏设计强调最小化带宽使用，并通过简单架构实现高效性能。服务器使用Golang编写，主要组件包括棋盘、客户端管理器、小地图聚合器和磁盘状态处理器。棋盘状态以8000x8000的数组存储，每个连接用户有一个goroutine负责处理数据传输和压缩。游戏还具有小地图、缩放等功能，并通过Nginx反向代理和Cloudflare进行部署。

主要讨论点：关于“One Million Chessboards”项目的技术实现、优化、自动化参与及项目背景的讨论

不同观点：
• 关于“Rooklyn”和“Queens”是否为不可摧毁的结构，有用户[butlike]最初表示困惑，认为可以通过攻击对方来摧毁结构，但随后理解了作者设置的规则，即棋子不能跨棋盘攻击，因此在这些规则下，这些结构是不可摧毁的。
• 用户[omoikane]关心是否有自动化机器人参与游戏，并提到类似项目“One Million Checkboxes”中曾有自动化工具进行动画处理。该用户认为机器人参与可以解决冷启动问题，但也可能影响人类玩家的参与。
• 用户[commandlinefan]赞赏项目对计算资源的高效利用，并提出优化的重要性，批评了一些低效的实现方式，认为云迁移应更加关注效率与实际成本之间的关系。
• 用户[mannyv]建议通过使用Cloudflare缓存静态数据以节省带宽，提出了类似视频帧差分的技术方案，认为通过只发送差异数据可以优化网络传输。
• 用户[dangoodmanUT]分享了其在类似项目UltimateArcade中的经验，强调了单线程优化和连续内存块操作的优势，认为这种方法可以提高效率。
• 用户[CJefferson]讨论了游戏状态回滚的问题，提出是否可以通过在冲突发生时直接从服务器获取最新状态来简化处理，同时指出了潜在的竞争条件问题。
• 用户[dvoros]表示对项目技术实现的赞赏，并提到自己正在开发类似项目，可能会借鉴该项目的某些想法，如使用Protobuf进行数据传输。
• 用户[sehansen]对项目中棋子状态框的星际争霸风格设计表示喜爱。
• 用户[heroku]提出了一种游戏规则的修改建议，即玩家只能在移动到其他棋盘后，从该棋盘进行攻击。
• 用户[topato]对项目背后的动机和变现模式表示好奇，质疑项目是否只是某个拥有大量空闲时间的大型科技公司工程师的个人项目。

补充讨论：
• 项目的技术优化，特别是带宽和计算资源的使用效率是讨论的一个重点。
• 自动化的参与和游戏规则的修改是另一个受到关注的方面，尤其是自动化工具对游戏体验的影响。
• 对项目背后动机的讨论显示出部分用户对现代软件工程师工作环境和项目变现压力的反思。

争议焦点：
• 主要集中在游戏规则的设计和机器人参与对游戏体验的影响上，部分用户认为机器人可以解决冷启动问题，但也有用户担心这会影响人类玩家的参与积极性。

44541088.article_content:
Running a million-board chess MMO in a single process
How One Million Chessboards works
Jun 24, 2025
One Million Chessboards
is a 1000x1000 grid of chess boards. Moving a piece moves it for everyone, instantly. There are no turns, and pieces can move between boards.
Loading...
making some moves
In the 10 days after launch, over 150,000 players made over 15,000,000 moves and hundreds of millions of queries. The game runs out of a single process that I didn’t touch over those 10 days
1
.
1
Once activity died down I bounced the server, reset the game, and started
experimenting with rule tweaks.
Making this project taught me a lot. It’s the first time I’ve used protobufs or
golang
, the first time I’ve measured nanoseconds, and my first time writing
rollback netcode
.
Let me tell you about it.
read the code here
play the game here
this essay is also a video on my youtube channel, if that’s more your style
Basics
Here’s a quick overview of the site before we jump into the details.
Rules
Pieces can move between boards
- I wanted one global game, not a million simultaneous ones
2
.
2
This seemed to really disappoint actual chess players. I’m a little surprised
by that - I don’t think that a million simultaneous games would lead to
particularly interesting gameplay! - but maybe I’m wrong.
Loading...
moving between boards
This meant that sharding the boards over many processes wasn’t free because those processes would need to communicate.
There are
no turns
. I didn’t think asking the whole internet to take turns would work well. And I thought real-time chess would be fun.
Loading...
taking a king
This meant that speed mattered; I needed to make sure that clients could make moves fast.
I prevented pieces from
capturing
pieces on other boards
. This was originally to prevent a queen from immediately capturing the king on the board above or below her, but ended up producing fun emergent gameplay as people (ab)used it to make indestructible structures like Rooklyn and Queens.
Rooklyn, Queens, and a digital monument
This rule was interesting, but it locked up the game. After activity died down I tried relaxing the restriction to only apply to unmoved pieces. I think this was a mistake - the original version was likely better.
The site has some other fun features. You can click on pieces to see how many times they’ve moved or captured a piece, there’s a minimap that lets you quickly jump to anywhere on the grid, and you can zoom out to see an overview of a larger chunk of the board at once.
Loading...
15 moves and 14 captures for this queen - not bad!
System Design Goals
Last year I built a surprisingly popular site called
One Million Checkboxes
. I learned a lot while
scaling it to handle load
; those learnings directly lead to my design goals.
I wanted to
minimize bandwidth
since it was my one unbounded cost. It’s very stressful going to bed not knowing what you’ll owe when you wake up.
I chose to run in a
single process
- partially because it was easier than sharding, partially because it was a fun challenge, but primarily because I was still smarting from a Hacker News
comment
(correctly!) pointing out that could have run One Million Checkboxes in a single process (instead of the 8 vms and a database).
This irked me because they were *right*
I aimed to be
bottlenecked by syscalls or message serialization
overhead. Both of those operations parallelize well, which means I could scale vertically to address them if I needed to.
And finally, I wanted to be
surprisingly fast
. My biggest gripe with most One Million Checkboxes clones is that they have too many loading spinners (One Million Checkboxes sent all its data to all clients which - when it wasn’t crashing - kept things snappy). I couldn’t ship
all
my data to clients this time so they’d have to load data occasionally - but I wanted to be faster than anyone would reasonably expect.
Basic Architecture
The server runs in a single golang process. It sits behind an nginx reverse proxy that sits behind cloudflare. An auxiliary VM handles metrics collection and stores backups of the game state. The frontend is written in React.
metrics are handled via vector and loki
The server has 4 core components - the board, client manager, minimap aggregator, and board to disk handler.
yes, they're all arrays, what of it
The board
is a dense 8000x8000 array of uint64s representing pieces.
The client manager
tracks the location of each client
The minimap aggregator
summarizes where pieces are
The board to disk handler
duplicates our board state and regularly serializes that state to disk
The server also has a set of goroutines (go’s lightweight threads) for every connected user. These goroutines track per-client data, accept moves, and are responsible for compressing and sending data to each client:
I regret calling this 'client' since it sounds like I'm referring to the website
The client has a few more responsibilities like assigning you a starting location next to another active pla

data.title: Unlike ChatGPT, Anthropic has doubled down on Artifacts
data.author: bewal416
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了Dropbox在2010年代通过云计算功能实现强大网络效应的成功，并将其与AI市场中的类似现象进行比较。文章首先回顾了Dropbox通过免费层和简便的文件共享吸引用户，然后分析了OpenAI和Anthropic在AI领域的不同策略。OpenAI推出了定制GPT功能，但之后似乎放弃了这一方向。而Anthropic则通过其“Artifacts”功能让用户无需编码即可创建AI驱动的应用程序，并解决了API认证和费用问题，实现了用户增长和经济效益的双赢。文章认为Anthropic的策略不仅技术上令人印象深刻，而且商业上也非常聪明，使Claude成为AI时代的Dropbox，为市场提供了实际价值。最后，文章还展望了未来通过与支付系统合作，进一步简化应用货币化的可能性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕不同AI工具（如Claude、OpenAI的Custom GPTs、Artifacts等）的实用性、成本和用户体验的讨论。

不同观点：
• **对Claude订阅和成本的看法**：
  - [graphememes] 认为Claude的API超时增加和使用成本过高，转而使用更便宜且性能相当的其他模型，因此取消了订阅。
  - [zebix86] 认为Claude在聊天界面上表现优异，可能更多针对普通用户而非开发工具整体产品线。

• **对OpenAI放弃Custom GPTs的看法**：
  - [esafak] 对OpenAI在Spring ‘24更新后基本放弃Custom GPTs表示不解，认为这应是OpenAI解决的问题，而不是用户的。
  - [PeterStuer] 猜测Custom GPTs只是营销策略，用来免费推广并获取商业发展线索，但效果不如预期。
  - [MagicMoonlight] 认为Custom GPTs只是不可见的提示词包装，没有实质区别，不值得关注。

• **对Artifacts功能的看法**：
  - [oidar] 对Artifacts的功能持怀疑态度，认为其在小规模代码时有用，但代码量大时变得笨重，无法单独编辑一行。
  - [danieltanfh95] 认为Artifacts能有效减少Token使用，提升对话轮次，并减少AI心理问题，如HALO式暴走或上下文中毒。
  - [jasonjmcghee] 曾经因为Artifacts的多种问题（如错误更新代码、无效编辑等）而关闭该功能，认为不值得。
  - [oc1] 对Anthropic的Artifacts产品策略表示怀疑，认为其重复OpenAI在GPT Marketplace上的错误，导致用户决策疲劳和失望。

补充讨论：
• **对Claude Code和Artifacts市场前景的看法**：
  - [bl4kers] 对将Claude比作Dropbox表示疑问，暗示可能并非褒奖。
  - [Shindi] 认为Claude在构建和分享上的易用性优于Custom GPTs，并提到人们在GPT商店 hackathon上对定制GPT感到失望。
  - [yshunnar] 赞同Claude的新战略，认为认证和支付是用户锁定的关键功能。
  - [mxwsn] 对是否有出色的Artifacts表示好奇，希望看到实例。

争议焦点：
• **Custom GPTs和Artifacts的实用性和市场价值**：一方认为这些功能简化了用户体验并提供更多选择，另一方则认为这些功能笨重、不实用，且导致用户决策疲劳和失望。

44577171.article_content:
Back in high school, I remember receiving an email for a study guide from a friend. Instead of the PDF coming attached to the email, it was a link to a site called Dropbox.
Upon opening the file, you create an account. From there you’re introduced to a feature stack that went well beyond any typical PDF: shared collaboration, comments, version history… the benefits of cloud computing- all within the familiarity of a PDF!
Dropbox achieved strong
network effects
in the 2010s due to generous free tiers, easy file sharing, and one-click account creation. Last year, I wrote
a blog post
on network effects, guessing if (and how) they would be brought into the AI market. In the post, I argued two points:
OpenAI began flirting with network-driven growth by introducing Custom GPTs in November 2023, and even more so when making them accessible to free users in May 2024.
AI companies might not
need
network effects to succeed, as user-generated content might not be what incrementally improves these tools (rather, artificial content, better memory, & great UX)
The rest of this post will be a follow-up of #1. In short, OpenAI appears to have
basically abandoned Custom GPTs
since their Spring ‘24 update, and I’m a bit stumped as to why. Sure, engagement might have been low, or a desire to shift the product team to other features like Canvas, improved memory, Deep Research, and Apple Intelligence integration. But, one would think that the allure of network effects would drive any consumer tech startup to continue toying with the idea!
Meanwhile, Anthropic’s Claude has been quietly pursuing a more powerful way for users to build for other users. Two months after the Custom GPT release,
Claude announced Artifacts
, allowing users to create single-page HTML apps, among other things. Artifacts became a hit within the tech community, potentially mainstreaming “vibe coding” for the first time. Writer Simon Willison (or dare I say,
fellow
writer)
became quite obsessed with Artifacts
over the past year.
Unlike ChatGPT, Anthropic has doubled down on Artifacts, making it more reliable and accessible to users. And in June 2025, they went
big
. Anthropic announced that Artifacts can now become AI-powered:
Today, we’re introducing […] the ability to embed AI capabilities directly into your creations—transforming artifacts into interactive, AI-powered apps.
Artifacts turn anyone into an app creator—no coding needed. Just tell Claude your idea to instantly create shareable apps, tools, and games.
Here’s their announcement video of a drum-making kit. You’ll see that the drum kit users can “Describe [a] beat” in the Claude-powered search bar.
It’s pretty cool! But, wouldn’t the creator need to worry about API authentication? Then, users abusing their credits? Or entering abusive prompts that would flag their account? It appears not.
Here’s
what makes this announcement newsworthy:
Claude [turns] artifacts into AI-powered apps, where the economics actually work for sharing.
When someone uses your Claude-powered app:
They authenticate with their existing Claude account
Their API usage counts against
their
subscription, not yours
You pay nothing for their usage
No one needs to manage API keys
While technically impressive, I find this to be an oddly brilliant business strategy for the prosperity of the Claude Chatbot- especially when Ben Thompson himself
categorized it as non-focus for Anthropic
. As an Artifact creator, I can infinitely extend the power of my Artifact at zero risk; all my users need is a Claude account.
Claude is the Dropbox of the Gen AI era.
It’s providing real value to the market for the return of user acquisition and CLV- something that its competitors are incapable or avoidant of doing.
Coding is the easiest part
One week before this Artifacts update, the father of vibe coding himself, Andrej Karpathy, went on stage to deliver a talk about the continued shifts in software development.
At the end
, Andrej shared that while the “coding” step of app development is easier than ever, getting to that last mile of production deployment still exists:
While Claude Artifacts are still in this “toyish” phase of single-page web apps, you can’t help but be in awe at all the things it solved on this slide: LLM API keys, Deployments, and Authentication. And no one needs to pay an Enterprise license to make it happen.
After Karpathy’s talk, I spent most of my time thinking about “Payments”. How hard would it be for a PayPal or Link to partner with a v0 or Lovable? I could see a future where vibe coded apps can be locked behind a paywall with one click- making apps as easy to monetize as a Gumroad product. I suppose pricing tiers would complicate things, but hey, there’s nothing code can’t solve!
Perhaps I’m romanticizing the tech ecosystem- Google can do everything on Andrej’s slide. Maybe that’s what
Sundar will task Varun and Douglas
to do.
44577171.article_summary: 本文讨论了Dropbox在2010年代通过云计算功能实现强大网络效应的成功，并将其与AI市场中的类似现象进行比较。文章首先回顾了Dropbox通过免费层和简便的文件共享吸引用户，然后分析了OpenAI和Anthropic在AI领域的不同策略。OpenAI推出了定制GPT功能，但之后似乎放弃了这一方向。而Anthropic则通过其“Artifacts”功能让用户无需编码即可创建AI驱动的应用程序，并解决了API认证和费用问题，实现了用户增长和经济效益的双赢。文章认为Anthropic的策略不仅技术上令人印象深刻，而且商业上也非常聪明，使Claude成为AI时代的Dropbox，为市场提供了实际价值。最后，文章还展望了未来通过与支付系统合作，进一步简化应用货币化的可能性。

data.author: brson
data.article_summary: 文章纪念了Gemini项目公开发布六周年。作者承认过去一年在geminiprotocol.net上活动较少，未能在特定纪念日更新内容，但对解决未决规范问题仍有计划和想法。作者承诺在未来某个日期前完成，但对此保持幽默和谨慎。同时，作者决定不再报告Geminispace规模统计，因为无限制增长并非项目目标。尽管个人近期较为懒散，但社区仍积极贡献，修正文档错误和翻译。作者对所有持续维护相关服务的人表示感谢。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Gemini协议的优缺点及其社区与技术实现的争议

不同观点：
• **对Gemini协议失去兴趣的观点**（vascocosta）：早期开发者，认为Gemini过于简化，尤其是强制加密和引入Gemtext格式，与个人追求的极简主义不符。同时，Gemini的内容面较窄，导致其兴趣减退。
• **对Gemini协议的批评与比较**（floren）：认为Gemini像是简化版的HTTP，但其设计有缺陷，例如“故意损坏的Markdown”和不必要的MIME类型支持。最终，Gemini可能逐渐与HTTP趋同，质疑其存在的必要性。
• **对Gemini的有限支持与开发体验**（NoboruWataya）：虽然认为Gemini开发简单有趣，但协议简化并未带来足够的内容。支持使用Markdown替代Gemtext，并对社区中的一些“价值观”争议有所提及。
• **支持Gemini的成就与实用性**（rickcarlino）：肯定Gemini作为一个新的网络协议，虽然用户基础小，但已解决了一些隐私和资源浪费的问题，且有实际应用和内容。
• **对Gemini生态而非协议的批评**（rcarmo）：认为Gemini的协议本身尚可，但生态系统不完善，尤其是内容创建的双重格式支持麻烦，支持使用Markdown。
• **对Gemini社区和协议的正面评价**（fishgoesblub）：对Gemini项目的存在表示赞赏，尽管自己不常使用。
• **对Gemini协议的神秘感与技术实现的疑问**（zozbot234）：质疑为何不直接使用HTTPS并通过MIME类型实现Gemini功能，或者直接在客户端禁止JS和CSS。
• **对Gemini带来的独特网络氛围的喜爱**（martinrue, debo_）：认为Gemini提供了与现代广告和AI充斥的互联网截然不同的体验，社区友好且具有90年代的网络氛围，同时强调匿名性和纯粹的内容体验。
• **对Gemini协议安全性的担忧**（Wild_Dolphins）：认为Gemini的强制禁止追踪和剥削用户的设计理念虽然值得赞赏，但可能引入浏览器端的攻击向量，尤其是考虑到主流Gemini浏览器的代码审计不足。

补充讨论：
• **技术实现的简化与扩展的矛盾**：一些评论者（如floren和rcarmo）认为Gemini过度简化，且最终会与HTTP趋同，质疑其独特性。
• **内容和社区氛围的局限性**：部分用户（如vascocosta和NoboruWataya）提到Gemini的内容面较窄，尤其是技术/自由软件（FOSS）相关内容较多，限制了用户的广泛兴趣。
• **对协议安全和隐私的关注**：Wild_Dolphins提出了对Gemini浏览器安全性的担忧，认为虽然协议本身强调隐私保护，但浏览器的实现可能存在安全隐患。
• **对Gemini协议的未来和实用性的不同看法**：一些用户（如rickcarlino和vouaobrasil）对Gemini的潜力和现有价值表示肯定，而另一些用户（如vascocosta和floren）则对其未来持怀疑态度。

争议焦点：
• **Gemtext与Markdown的格式选择**：多个评论者提到Gemtext不如Markdown方便，质疑为何不直接使用Markdown。
• **Gemini协议的必要性与独特性**：部分用户认为Gemini与HTTP过于相似，质疑其作为新协议的必要性。
• **Gemini浏览器的安全性与社区的“价值观”争议**：部分用户对Gemini浏览器的安全性表示担忧，并对社区中的一些“价值观”讨论有所保留。

44578143.article_content:
2025-06-20 - Six years of Gemini!
Today is the sixth anniversary of the public announcement of Project Gemini!
It's been a quiet year at geminiprotocol.net thus far.  I've let two "Apollo days" slip by without a word.  I'm about as disappointed in myself for this as I expect many folks are unsurprised by it.  I do still have plans and clear ideas for finalising the minor oustanding spec issues.  I'd tell people to look forward to something by Apollo 15 day (2025-11-03), but at this point, who'd believe me?  Well, let's see.
I'll stick to my promise from last year's anniversary announcement of discontinuing the previously traditional report of Geminispace size statistics: endless growth is not and never was a goal of the project, so there's little sense in continuing to do this.  In case anybody thinks this is just a high-minded way to disguise the first set of disappointing numbers, I did check and in fact almost all of them have gone up a little, so there.
I might have been idle of late, but not everybody in the community has been.  I continue to receive, and to apply, patches to the geminiprotocol.net repository correcting errors in the official documentation or adding translations of into diverse languages, and I continue to be very grateful for these generous contributions of time and energy.  The same is true, of course, for all those folks who continue to keep search engines, aggregators, multi-user hosting services and more up and running, year after year.  Thank you all!

data.author: shawa_a_a
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对开源软件、旧软件应用的维护与使用，以及对具体应用（如Duolingo、Anki）的评价与技术探讨

不同观点：
• WeirderScience认为SourceForge在保存旧的开源软件（OSS）网站和代码库方面做出了贡献，尽管其广告和恶意软件问题令人诟病。
• aaronbrethorst澄清了一个技术细节，指出符号“-”和“+”用于区分实例方法和类方法，而不是表示公有或私有。他通过自己2003年发布的Mac OS X应用作为例子来支持这一观点。
• Cockbrand以讽刺的语气评论了文章中对Duolingo的讨论，暗示其内容有不准确之处，并提到德国一个众所周知的文化趣闻来佐证其观点。
• johnisgood表达了对旧OS X应用iWeb的喜爱，分享了个人经历，表明其在12岁时曾使用过该应用。
• shawa_a_a重新尝试使用Anki并深入研究了其功能，分享了关于Anki使用细节的文档链接，并对其功能进行了正面评价。他认为理解这些细节比依赖感觉判断（如“暂停 before answering”）更有价值。
• asterios33对图标扁平化和灰暗色调的设计选择表示不满，但没有进一步解释原因。
• matsemann对旧软件无法直接运行表示遗憾，并提到在Windows上可以运行旧的exe文件，暗示对Mac平台的兼容性问题感到不满。
• GuinansEyebrows表达了对旧软件的喜爱，并期待一个现代的、原生的‘jared, the butcher of song’版本能够在macOS上发布。
• kreelman欣赏网站的早期网络风格，并提出将相关内容转化为PWA（渐进式网络应用）以便跨平台运行的建议。
• busymom0认为网站的复古外观导致可读性差，并分享了通过Safari的阅读模式解决此问题的经验。她还提到自己曾接手并复活了一个14年前的Objective-C iPhone应用，表示愿意帮助解决相关技术问题。
• treetalker识别出文中所讨论的Genius.app，并提供了其代码库链接，同时对比了Duolingo和Anki，指出Anki缺乏精确的反馈机制。
• brnt推荐了一款荷兰软件Overhoor，分享了自己在Windows 3.11和Windows ME时代使用该软件的经历，并指出该软件在Wine中也能运行，表达了对旧软件的怀旧之情。
• TMWNN提到自己依赖一个2010年的Intel应用，并担心Rosetta停止支持后该应用无法运行，暗示对旧软件的长期依赖问题。

补充讨论：
• 对旧软件的怀旧情感和技术细节的讨论较为突出，尤其是对旧OS X应用和开源软件的维护与使用。
• Anki的功能和使用细节成为技术讨论的焦点，有用户对其进行了正面评价并提供了详细的使用建议。
• 设计美学上的争议，如图标扁平化和网站背景对可读性的影响，也成为讨论的一部分。
• 对旧软件兼容性和现代化需求的关注，尤其是对macOS平台上旧应用的支持问题。

争议焦点：
• Duolingo的文章描述是否准确，以及Anki是否缺乏精确的反馈机制成为讨论中的争议点。

data.title: Algorithms for making interesting organic simulations
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary:
本文介绍了用于生成有机形态模拟的算法，重点在于艺术表现而非科学意义。主要包括：

1. **Physarum算法**（Jeff Jones，2010）：模拟如多头绒泡菌的行为。基本原理是“粒子”在二维空间移动，留下轨迹并倾向于跟随轨迹。算法步骤包括感知、旋转与移动、沉积轨迹，以及轨迹扩散与衰减。通过调整四个主要参数（传感器距离、传感器角度、旋转角度、移动距离），可以产生不同的模拟效果。

2. **Sage Jenson的36 Points项目**（2019-2022）：基于Physarum算法的复杂版本，每个“点”对应不同的参数组合，产生多样行为。关键在于根据轨迹图的值动态调整参数，使参数随位置变化，增加了算法的复杂性和表现力。

通过这些算法，可以创建复杂的有机形态模拟，用于艺术和视觉效果创作。

44551777.article_content:
Algorithms for making interesting organic simulations
The purpose of this article is to explain techiques that enabled me to make simulations like the one
below, along with a lot of other organic looking things. We will focus on algorithmic techniques for
artistic purpose
rather than scientific meaning.
1. Physarum algorithm from Jeff Jones (2010)
Jeff Jones presented a simulation algorithm that reproduces the behavior of organisms such
as
Physarum polycephalum
.
It is explained in
this
paper
.
Results typically look like this:
(source: screenshots from implementation by Amanda
Ghassaei)
General principle
The basic idea is that particles (also called agents) move around, leaving a trail behind them and trying
to follow the trails
they detect.
Below is an interactive explanation of a single agent,
without representing the trail update
.
Please don't mind the glitch after slider change :)
Detailed description of the algorithm
A large number of agents move in a 2D space.
At each iteration of the algorithm, agents deposit trail on an
image called a
trail map
, just by adding a value to a pixel of the image. In the above
illustration, each cell represents a pixel of the trail map image.
Agent attributes:
2D position
(x,y)
orientation: an
angle
called
heading
Here are the different steps for an iteration of the algorithm:
1. Sensing:
Each agent "looks" at three places: straight ahead, slightly right, and slightly
left.
sometimes not so slightly
The distance from the agent to the 3 sensor places is defined by the parameter
Sensor
Distance
(SD)
.
The side angle is a parameter called
Sensor Angle
(SA)
.
The agent detects the trail intensity at those three positions/pixels.
2. Rotation and movement:
If the highest value is to the left or right, the agent turns in that direction.
The turn angle is controlled by the parameter
Rotation Angle
(RA)
.
If the highest value is straight ahead, the agent doesn't rotate.
Actually in the case where straight ahead is the lowest value, the agent makes a random choice
between left and right.
After potentially turning, the agent moves forward by a distance called
Move Distance
(MD)
.
3. Deposit:
the agents add a value to the trail map at their new position.
4. Trail diffusion and decay:
At each iteration, after deposit of all agents, the trail is slightly diffused (a sort of blur effect on
the image), and multiplied by a
decay factor
(for example
0.75
) to
keep things stable. A more precise
explanation will be given later.
Although the trail is a 2D
image,
artistically it's often better not to display it directly, and instead only show the
particles.
By modifying the four main parameters (SD, SA, RA, MD), various simulated behaviors can be observed.
The algorithm from Jeff Jones can have more complex features than this but I'm giving a simple version
that's used for what is described next in this article.
Real interactive implementation with few agents.
The simulation below implements the algorithm, there are just too few particles and too few pixels for
cool
structures to appear!
You can check out
this
very nice webpage
by Amanda Ghassaei, to see the simulation with a lot of particles and with
controllable sliders.
Another explanation/review of this algorithm from Jeff Jones can be found
here
. It has a pretty drawing to sum up
the algorithm.
Show explanation image by Sage Jenson
2.
36 Points
by Sage Jenson (2019-2022)
A more complex version of the previous algorithm can be found in the work
36 Points
by Sage Jenson, which
displays amazing varied behaviours. Press letters or digits of your keyboard to
change the Point.
26 letters + 10 digits = 36
It uses a single algorithm and each Point represents different parameters, which result
in different behaviours.
A Point corresponds to a behaviour obtained with 20 parameters (so mathematically this project shows 36
points of ℝ²⁰).
The above images show 6 Points.
(found there)
Main idea
Looking at the code we can understand some clever ideas. The most important one is to make the parameters
of the classic algorithm different depending on the value
\( x \)
of the trail map at
the particle's position.
The formulas below are used:
$$
\begin{eqnarray}
\text{sensor distance} &=& p_1 + p_2 \cdot x^{p_3} \nonumber \\
\text{sensor angle} &=& p_4 + p_5 \cdot x^{p_6} \nonumber \\
\text{rotation angle} &=& p_7 + p_8 \cdot x^{p_9} \nonumber \\
\text{move distance} &=& p_{10} + p_{11} \cdot x^{p_{12}}
\end{eqnarray}
$$
For each iteration, we first get the value
\( x \)
of the trail map at the particle's
position,
and then with the previous formulas we just do the same as the previous classic algorithm. That gives us
12
parameters to play with instead of 4.
Below is an update of the animated explanation with a single agent. This is using fixed parameters.
I think adding interactive sliders to control the 12 parameters wouldn't add much value for the
explanation.

data.title: The Symbol Grounding Problem (1990)
data.author: Fibra
data.article_summary:
本文讨论了符号接地问题（Symbol Grounding Problem）：符号系统中的符号如何获得内在意义，而不仅仅依赖于人类头脑中的意义。纯粹的符号模型仅基于符号的外形进行操作，缺乏内在语义。作者斯蒂文·哈纳德提出，符号表征必须通过两种非符号表征进行自下而上的接地：一是对近端感官投影的模拟（ iconic representations），二是对对象和事件类别不变特征的检测（categorical representations）。连接主义（connectionism）可以通过学习这些不变特征，将名称与它们所代表的对象联系起来，从而解决符号接地问题。符号操作不仅应基于符号的任意形状，还应基于其感官表征中的非任意形状。这种混合模型将符号功能视为从类别名称的接地中自然浮现的结果，而非纯粹符号模型的对手。

关键词：符号系统，连接主义，类别学习，认知模型，神经模型

主要讨论点：Harnad的论文及其关于符号系统标准的争议

不同观点：
• MarkusQ认为Harnad的论文设定过于严苛的标准，导致许多数学和逻辑领域被排除在外。具体批评包括：  
  - Harnad要求符号系统的规则必须完全是符号性的。  
  - 要求所有元素都必须具有“语义可解释性”。  
  - 忽略符号之间的关系，从而排除了诸如矩阵乘法、几何等领域。  
  MarkusQ认为，这种严格的标准实际上是Harnad自己制造问题，然后再尝试解决。

• jstrebel则对该论文持积极态度，认为这篇论文没有得到应有的关注。他们指出：  
  - 当前大家对LLMs（大型语言模型）的狂热忽视了其基础的不稳定性（如训练数据中毒问题）。  
  - 目前缺乏基于标志性和分类表征的AI系统实际应用，这令人遗憾。

补充讨论：
• MarkusQ的批评集中在Harnad对符号系统的定义过于狭隘，导致许多重要的数学和逻辑概念无法纳入讨论。
• jstrebel则关注论文所揭示的AI基础问题以及实际应用的不足，认为这些问题的探讨具有重要价值。

争议焦点：
• Harnad对符号系统的高标准是否合理，特别是这些标准是否会导致排除大量数学和逻辑领域的有效内容。
• 当前AI研究（如LLMs）是否忽视了基础理论问题，以及是否需要更多基于不同表征方式的实际应用。

Harnad, S. (1990) The Symbol Grounding Problem. Physica D 42: 335-346.
THE SYMBOL GROUNDING PROBLEM
Stevan Harnad
Department of Psychology
Princeton University
Princeton NJ 08544
harnad@cogsci.soton.ac.uk
ABSTRACT:
There has been much discussion
recently about the scope and
limits of purely symbolic models of the mind and about the proper role
of connectionism in cognitive modeling. This paper describes the
"symbol grounding problem": How can the semantic interpretation of a
formal symbol system be made
intrinsic to the system, rather than just parasitic on the meanings in
our heads? How can the meanings of the meaningless symbol tokens,
manipulated solely on the basis of their (arbitrary) shapes, be
grounded in anything but other meaningless symbols? The problem is
analogous to trying to learn Chinese from a Chinese/Chinese dictionary
alone. A candidate solution is sketched: Symbolic representations must
be grounded bottom-up in nonsymbolic representations of two kinds:  (1)
"iconic representations" , which are analogs of the proximal sensory
projections of distal objects and events, and (2)
"categorical representations" , which are learned and innate
feature-detectors that pick out the invariant features of object and
event categories from their sensory projections. Elementary symbols are
the names of these object and event categories, assigned on the basis
of their (nonsymbolic) categorical representations. Higher-order (3)
"symbolic representations" , grounded in these elementary symbols,
consist of symbol strings describing category membership relations
(e.g., "An X is a Y that is Z").
Connectionism is one natural candidate for the mechanism that learns
the invariant features underlying categorical representations, thereby
connecting names to the proximal projections of the distal objects they
stand for. In this way connectionism can be seen as a complementary
component in a hybrid nonsymbolic/symbolic model of the mind, rather
than a rival to purely symbolic modeling. Such a hybrid model would not
have an autonomous symbolic "module," however; the symbolic functions
would emerge as an intrinsically "dedicated" symbol system as a
consequence of the bottom-up grounding of categories' names in their
sensory representations. Symbol manipulation would be governed not just
by the arbitrary shapes of the symbol tokens, but by the nonarbitrary
shapes of the icons and category invariants in which they are grounded.
KEYWORDS:
symbol systems, connectionism, category learning, cognitive
models, neural models
1. Modeling the Mind
1.1 From Behaviorism to Cognitivism
For many years the only
empirical approach in psychology was behaviorism, its only explanatory
tools input/input and input/output associations (in the case of
classical conditioning; Turkkan 1989) and the reward/punishment history
that "shaped" behavior (in the case of operant conditioning; Catania &
Harnad 1988). In a reaction against the subjectivity of armchair
introspectionism, behaviorism had declared that it was just as illicit
to theorize about what went on in the
head of the organism to generate its behavior as to theorize about
what went on in its
mind. Only observables were to be the subject matter of psychology;
and, apparently, these were expected to explain themselves.
Psychology became more like an empirical science when, with the gradual
advent of cognitivism (Miller 1956, Neisser 1967, Haugeland 1978), it
became acceptable to make inferences about the
unobservable processes underlying behavior.
Unfortunately, cognitivism let mentalism in again
by the back door too, for the hypothetical internal processes came
embellished with subjective interpretations. In fact, semantic interpretability
(meaningfulness),
as we shall see, was one of the defining features of the most prominent
contender vying to become the theoretical vocabulary of cognitivism,
the "language of thought" (Fodor 1975), which became the prevailing
view in cognitive theory for several decades in the form of the
"symbolic" model of the mind: The mind is a symbol system and cognition
is symbol manipulation. The possibility of generating complex behavior
through symbol manipulation was empirically demonstrated by successes
in the field of artificial intelligence (AI).
1.2 Symbol Systems
What is a symbol system? From Newell (1980) Pylyshyn (1984), Fodor
(1987) and the classical work of Von Neumann, Turing, Goedel, Church,
etc. (see Kleene 1969) on the foundations of computation, we can
reconstruct the following definition:
A symbol system is:
a set of arbitrary
"physical tokens" scratches on paper, holes on a tape, events in a
digital computer, etc. that are
manipulated on the basis of "explicit rules" that are
likewise physical tokens and strings of tokens. The rule-governed
symbol-token manipulation is based

Clippy 📎
Copy files from your terminal that actually paste into GUI apps. No more switching to Finder.
macOS only
- built specifically for the Mac clipboard system.
Why Clippy?
pbcopy
copies file
contents
, but GUI apps need file
references
. When you
pbcopy < image.png
, you can't paste it into Slack or email - those apps expect files, not raw bytes. Your only option is to leave the terminal and drag files from Finder.
Clippy bridges this gap by detecting what you want and using the right clipboard format:
#
Copy files as references (for pasting into GUI apps)
clippy report.pdf
#
⌘V into any app - uploads the file
clippy
*
.jpg
#
Multiple files at once
#
Copy piped/streamed data as files
curl -s https://picsum.photos/300
|
clippy
#
Download → clipboard as file
cat archive.tar.gz
|
clippy
#
Pipe → paste as file
#
Smart detection for text files
clippy notes.txt
#
Copies text content
echo
"
Hello
"
|
clippy
#
Works like pbcopy for piped text
Stay in your terminal. Copy anything. Paste anywhere.
Key Features
Smart detection
: Automatically decides whether to copy content or file references
File support
:
clippy document.pdf
copies the PDF as a file (not its raw content)
Multiple files
:
clippy *.jpg
copies all JPGs as file references
Binary streaming
: Pipe images/PDFs and paste them as files in other apps
Text handling
: Text files are copied as content, just like pbcopy
Automatic cleanup
: Temporary files from piped data are cleaned up intelligently
Installation
Homebrew (Recommended)
brew install neilberkman/clippy/clippy
Build from Source
#
Clone and build
git clone https://github.com/neilberkman/clippy.git
cd
clippy
go build -o clippy
.
sudo mv clippy /usr/local/bin/
#
Or use go install
go install github.com/neilberkman/clippy@latest
Usage
Basic Usage
#
Copy a file
clippy myfile.txt
#
Text content
clippy photo.jpg
#
File reference
#
Pipe data
echo
"
Hello, World!
"
|
clippy
cat image.png
|
clippy
Flags
clippy --verbose file.txt
#
Show success messages
clippy -v file.txt
#
Short version
Configuration
Create
~/.clippy.conf
for persistent settings:
#
Enable verbose output by default
verbose
= true
Features
Smart Detection
Text files
(
.txt
,
.md
, code files) → copies actual text
Binary files
(images, PDFs, zips) → copies as file reference
Works with both file arguments and piped input
Silent by Default
No output unless
--verbose
flag is used
Perfect for scripts and automation
Errors still shown on stderr
Automatic Cleanup
Temporary files created for piped binary data are managed automatically
Background process scans for orphaned temp files on each run
Checks if temp files are still referenced in clipboard before removal
Non-blocking - cleanup happens while main operation proceeds
How It Works
File Mode
(when you pass a filename):
Detects MIME type
Text files → reads content, copies as text
Other files → copies file path reference
Stream Mode
(when you pipe data):
Detects MIME type from content
Text data → copies as text
Binary data → saves to temp file, copies reference
Examples
#
Copy code file as text
clippy main.go
#
Copy PDF as file reference
clippy report.pdf
#
Copy command output
ls -la
|
clippy
#
Copy image from curl
curl -s https://picsum.photos/300
|
clippy
#
Silent operation for scripts
clippy data.txt
&&
echo
"
Copied!
"
#
Verbose mode to see what happened
clippy -v recording.mp4
Testing
#
Run tests
go
test
-v
#
Run with race detector
go
test
-race
Alternatives
gcopy
gcopy
is a cross-platform clipboard tool that also works with files. Key differences:
Cross-platform
: gcopy works on Linux/Windows, clippy is macOS-only
Implementation
: clippy uses native macOS APIs, gcopy uses AppleScript
File handling
: clippy copies file references (like Finder), gcopy copies file contents - this makes clippy work for pasting images/PDFs into apps, while gcopy doesn't
Multiple files
: clippy supports
*.jpg
, gcopy handles one file at a time
Cleanup
: clippy auto-cleans temp files, gcopy doesn't
Choose gcopy if you need cross-platform support. Choose clippy for better macOS integration and multi-file support.
Why "Clippy"?
Because it's a helpful clipboard assistant that knows what you want to do! 📎
License
MIT

data.title: Shipping WebGPU on Windows in Firefox 141
data.author: Bogdanp
data.article_summary: Firefox 141将发布WebGPU，为网页内容提供现代化的图形处理接口，支持高性能计算和渲染。WebGPU由W3C标准定义，Mozilla自2017年起参与其开发，目前已在Google Chrome和即将发布的Safari 26中实现。Firefox的WebGPU目前仅在Windows平台上推出，未来几个月将扩展至Mac、Linux和Android。Firefox的实现基于WGPU，这是一个Rust编写的开源项目，提供跨平台图形API接口。虽然性能和规范合规性仍有提升空间，但Firefox 141中的WebGPU已能顺利运行多数高可见度应用。用户可在遇到问题时通过Bugzilla报告。WebGPU的发布标志着Mozilla多年开发工作的成果，期待看到开发者利用其潜力。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：WebGPU的进展及其在不同平台和浏览器上的应用前景

不同观点：
• astlouis44对Firefox团队的进展表示兴奋，并提到其公司正在将Unreal引擎带到浏览器中，通过自定义WebGPU RHI实现。他还分享了相关演示链接，但指出仅在基于Chromium的浏览器和部分Android手机上有效。
• SaintSeiya认为现代图形API（如Vulkan、Metal、DirectX12）相比OpenGL时代并没有更易用或更跨平台，重新包装这些API是时间浪费，并批评了追求性能而牺牲易用性的做法。
• Vipitis提到使用wgpu两年来的经验，希望更多维护者参与以解决长期存在的问题，并指出wgpu-native绑定更新缓慢。
• coffeeaddict1希望WebGPU能在非Web场景中得到更多应用，认为目前除Rust社区外，对WebGPU的兴趣不大，且很多项目已使用自定义抽象层。
• JasperBekkers对WebGPU的推广感到高兴，因为这将使他们的gpu-allocator库被更广泛使用，并提到其在wgpu的DX12后端中的应用。

补充讨论：
• simonw发现WebGPU已在Firefox Nightly中支持macOS，并成功运行了相关演示，而在普通版Firefox中则不支持。
• bobajeff对WebGPU在Linux上的支持进展缓慢表示不满，认为这是由于浏览器安全攻击面问题，并批评了现代浏览器标准的复杂性。
• modeless推测Firefox可能比Chrome更早支持WebGPU在Linux上的实现。
• politelemon期待Linux实现，并询问值得尝试的WebGPU演示。
• pjmlp对WebGPU在更多浏览器中的支持表示欢迎，并提到Safari最近也启用了预览支持。
• grovesNL对WebGPU在Firefox中的支持表示兴奋和感谢。
• joelthelion质疑WebGPU的用例，担心其可能被用于利用用户硬件进行比特币挖矿。
• mclau157质疑是否有足够的开发者参与WebGPU的应用开发，并希望看到类似Flash开发者复兴的现象。
• danjl建议支持RTX光线追踪以提升WebGPU的实用性。
• pixelpoet对WebGPU的支持表示赞赏和期待。

争议焦点：
• WebGPU在不同平台和浏览器上的支持进度以及实际应用场景存在争议。部分用户对Linux支持的滞后表示不满，并对WebGPU的广泛应用前景持怀疑态度。
• 对于现代图形API的易用性和跨平台性存在不同看法，部分用户认为重新包装现代API是时间浪费，而另一些用户则对其前景表示乐观。

总结：讨论主要围绕WebGPU的技术进展、应用场景及其在不同平台上的支持情况展开，涉及用户对其前景的期待、技术实现的难点以及对浏览器标准复杂性的批评。

44579317.article_content:
jblandy
Uncategorized
July 15, 2025
2 Minutes
After years in development, we will be releasing WebGPU on Windows in Firefox 141! WebGPU gives web content a modern interface to the user’s graphics processor, enabling high-performance computation and rendering. We’re excited about WebGPU because we believe it will raise the ceiling for games, visualization, and local computation on the web.
You can find a tutorial on WebGPU at
webgpufundamentals.org
, try out the
WebGPU Samples
, and read documentation for the API at
MDN
. WebGPU is defined in two W3C standards,
WebGPU
and
WGSL
, whose development Mozilla has participated in since it began in 2017.
WebGPU has been available in Google Chrome since 2023, and is expected to be available in Safari 26 this fall.
Although Firefox 141 enables WebGPU only on Windows, we plan to ship WebGPU on Mac and Linux in the coming months, and finally on Android. Windows was our first priority because that’s where the great majority of our users are, but we are looking forward to enabling it on the other platforms as soon as it is robust and our test coverage is adequate. (Your humble author is strictly a Linux user, so this concern is close to his heart.) Note that WebGPU has been available in Firefox Nightly on all platforms other than Android for quite some time.
Firefox’s WebGPU implementation is based on
WGPU
, a Rust crate that provides a unified, portable interface to the low-level graphics APIs of the underlying platform:
Direct3D 12
,
Metal
, and
Vulkan
. WGPU is developed as an independent open source project on GitHub, but Mozilla is a major contributor. WGPU is widely used outside Firefox, and has an active community, so if you are a Rust developer interested in contributing to Firefox’s WebGPU support, WGPU is a good place to start.
WebGPU is a large, complex API. We’ve focused our efforts so far on making high-visibility WebGPU applications and demos run smoothly, and we believe it should work well in Firefox 141 for many use cases. However, there is plenty of work remaining to be done to improve our performance and compliance with the specification. In particular:
Firefox uses unbuffered inter-process communication to convey web content’s requests to the GPU sandbox process, which introduces significant overhead. We addressed this in
Bug 1968122
, which improved performance significantly. The fix will appear in Firefox 142.
Firefox currently uses an interval timer to tell when the GPU has completed a task, adding significant latency to many applications where the task finishes quickly. There are better ways to do this, we are changing Firefox to use them. You can follow our progress in
Bug 1870699
.
Firefox does not yet support WebGPU’s
importExternalTexture
method, which lets the GPU read decompressed video content directly from the decoder. You can follow our progress in
Bug 1827116
.
Please give WebGPU a try in Firefox! If you encounter problems, please report them in the
WebGPU component
in Bugzilla. As always, provide us with as detailed instructions as you can to make the bug occur, and attach the contents of
about:support
to the bug so we can see what kind of system you are using.
It’s been a big project, but we’re done tinkering with the engine and taking test drives — we’re finally ready to roll WebGPU out of the garage and hand it over to you for daily use. We’re looking forward to seeing what you can do with WebGPU in Firefox!

data.title: Hijacking Trust? Bitvise Under Fire for Controlling Domain of FOSS Project PuTTY
data.author: ColinWright
data.article_summary:
Bitvise因控制开源项目PuTTY相关域名putty.org而受到批评。尽管PuTTY是广受欢迎的SSH和Telnet客户端，其域名却由商业竞争对手Bitvise拥有。访问putty.org会看到对PuTTY的引用及官方下载链接，但同时 prominently 宣传Bitvise自己的SSH客户端。批评者认为这是误导性品牌宣传，利用了开源软件的公众信任。

更严重的是，Bitvise在被曝光后公开了与记者的邮件往来，包括记者的全名，且在其支持渠道中使用了侮辱性语言。Bitvise不仅未正面回应伦理问题，还通过技术性细节和哲学性解释回避批评。

此事件引发了关于数字责任和公众信任的讨论，强调了合法与合乎伦理之间的灰色地带。Bitvise尚未表示会放弃该域名。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：PuTTY相关网站的合法性及域名争议

不同观点：
• **反对putty.org作为官方网站**：
  - **asimops**：认为PuTTY的官方网站一直是https://www.chiark.greenend.org.uk/~sgtatham/putty/，从未改变。putty.org只是利用了名字，不应被视为官方网站。
  - **ptx**：指出putty.org从未属于PuTTY项目，用户误以为它是官方域名。搜索引擎如何处理域名的问题也被质疑。
  - **TRiG_Ireland**：观察到putty.org网站内容与软件无关，进一步质疑其关联性。

• **批评Bitvise及域名占用**：
  - **mnaimd**：批评Bitvise占用putty.org域名的行为，并指出许多成功的开源软件（如Linux、Git、GCC）都通过社区驱动发展，而非依赖单一所有者。
  - **greatgib**：认为Bitvise持有putty.org域名可能是寄生或误导行为，可能在某些国家的法律下不合法。

• **中立或支持Bitvise**：
  - **bstsb**：认为记者和Bitvise都有责任，Bitvise的不专业回应和错误使用markdown格式是问题，但putty.org从未历史性地与PuTTY项目关联。
  - **msgodel**：不认为Bitvise做错了什么，认为运行一个推广自己产品的粉丝网站是合理的。

• **支持当前情况**：
  - **fifteen1506**：认为这是一个非问题，putty.org链接到了正确的PuTTY网站，问题可能出在SEO上，而不是Bitvise的行为。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点**：putty.org是否应被视为PuTTY的官方网站，以及Bitvise持有该域名是否构成误导或不正当行为。
• **技术背景**：讨论涉及PuTTY软件的历史和开源软件的成功案例，以及SEO如何影响域名和网站的可见性。
• **其他意见**：有人提到Windows已具有原生的SSH客户端，质疑PuTTY的当前使用情况。

44579265.article_content:
Hijacking Trust? Bitvise Under Fire for Controlling Domain of Open-Source Project PuTTY
PupRed
bigtech
bitvise
domainsnatcher
putty
ssh
In the open-source world, trust, transparency, and community stewardship form the foundation of public credibility. But a recent case involving the domain name
putty.org
calls these values into question.
The domain, long associated by users with
PuTTY
, the widely-used open-source SSH and Telnet client, is not controlled by the PuTTY project itself — but by a commercial competitor:
Bitvise
.
Bitvise offers its own SSH client, and while their software is available free of charge, the company now faces criticism for its
appropriation of a domain name that clearly and historically signals the PuTTY project
— a project maintained for over two decades by developer
Simon Tatham
.
A visit to
putty.org
brings users to a page that references PuTTY, links to the official download site — but also prominently advertises Bitvise's own SSH client. Critics argue this amounts to misleading branding and exploitation of public trust in open-source software.
Update: Bitvise escalates with personal attack after publishing private correspondence
Following publication of this article, Bitvise took the unusual step of
publishing the entire email exchange with the journalist on their public support site
, including the journalist’s
full name without consent
— despite a clear request to anonymize or redact personal information.
When asked to censor the name, a Bitvise representative responded not with a correction, but with verbal abuse:
“Lol 😂 You fucking idiot.”
This statement — sent via the company’s official support channel — raises serious concerns not only about Bitvise’s domain practices, but also about its
conduct, professionalism, and treatment of individuals engaging in legitimate inquiry
.
The incident reflects a pattern: rather than addressing substantive criticism about its use of the
putty.org
domain, Bitvise has responded with deflection, hostility, and now a personal attack on a journalist — further distancing itself from the transparency and accountability expected in both commercial and open-source communities.
Requests for formal comment remain open.
“The PuTTY project never had this domain”
When approached for comment,
Bitvise’s response sidestepped the ethical questions entirely
, focusing instead on technicalities of ownership:
“The PuTTY project, or its author, did not originally own this domain. It is misleading to talk about 'returning' a domain which the PuTTY project never had,”
—
Denis Bider
, Bitvise representative
Asked whether Bitvise would consider transferring the domain to PuTTY’s actual maintainer, or whether they believed such use could be ethically problematic, Bider replied dismissively:
“What you dislike is that the page appears high in search results because it provides a useful service.”
He later escalated the tone further, stating:
“It speaks to the nature of someone's mind when the first thought that occurs to them is expropriation and confiscation.”
A question of ethics, not legality
While Bitvise claims no financial gain from the domain, the issue is not about profit, but
intentional association
. The choice to register
putty.org
— and use it to promote a product — inherently capitalizes on PuTTY’s reputation, regardless of whether revenue is generated directly.
Asked whether such use was ethically justifiable, Bitvise offered instead a philosophical statement:
“The difference is not one of profit, it is one of philosophy. You believe software can be managed by a committee. I believe software requires an owner, otherwise it is dead.”
Yet this framing ignores the core issue: controlling a domain name that misleads users into associating Bitvise’s product with the PuTTY project. It’s not about software governance — it’s about
public trust
and
digital responsibility
.
Exploiting visibility, eroding integrity
Search engines treat domain names like
putty.org
as authoritative. A user looking for the PuTTY project might easily assume they are visiting an official or affiliated site. That’s what makes Bitvise’s claim of providing a “service” ring hollow: the service comes wrapped in misleading branding that benefits the company at the expense of clarity.
Digital rights advocates argue that
just because a domain is legally available doesn’t mean it should be claimed
, especially when it mimics a widely known, community-driven project.
As the open-source community continues to grapple with questions of ownership, sustainability, and trust, this case serves as a potent example of how ethical lines can blur in the space between legality and legitimacy.
So far,
Bitvise has shown no sign of releasing the domain
— and no willingness to address the broader ethical dilemma behind their actions. Their responses raise a final question:
When a company benefits from the public’s confusion, is that smart business — or quiet deception?
Written by PuPRed.com - Last updated 13.J

data.title: Nextflow: System for creating scalable, portable, reproducible workflows
data.author: saikatsg
data.article_summary: Nextflow 是一个基于数据流编程模型的工作流系统，用于创建可扩展、可移植和可重现的计算管道。它简化了并行和分布式管道的编写，支持多种执行平台（如本地机器、HPC、AWS、Azure、Google Cloud、Kubernetes）和依赖管理工具（如Conda、Docker、Singularity）。安装简单，通过一行命令即可完成。Nextflow 拥有活跃的社区支持和详细的文档，并通过 nf-core 项目汇集高质量的工作流。该项目基于 Groovy 和 GPars 构建，使用 Apache 2.0 许可证发布。如果使用 Nextflow，需引用相关论文。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：不同工作流语言在生物信息学中的使用和优缺点比较（主要包括Nextflow、Snakemake和WDL）。

不同观点：
• totalperspectiv认为Nextflow和Snakemake是目前生物信息学中使用最多的工作流语言，WDL相对较少使用。他对Nextflow使用Groovy而非Scala表示遗憾，但对Nextflow的dsl3草案中引入的静态类型特性感到兴奋。

• Wintermute同样对Nextflow使用Groovy表示不满，但承认其在流行度上超过Snakemake，并将此归因于nf-core提供的一系列精选工作流。他还提到Nextflow会向HPC调度器提交大量单独的任务，导致问题，不过最新的阵列任务支持可能解决这一问题。

• armedgorilla分享了他们从Cromwell/WDL转向Argo的经验。他们选择Argo是因为其在K8s集群上运行良好，并且在生物信息学和机器学习团队中只需要维护一个编排工具。他们提到使用YAML配置对科学家来说有一定学习难度，但认为这与学习Groovy相似。

• trashpandato高度评价Nextflow，认为其在生物信息学工作中的重要性应被高度重视。

• azan_表示他一直使用Snakemake，并询问是否有同时熟悉Snakemake和Nextflow的人可以分享是否值得转向Nextflow。

• christopher8827提到在他的前一个生物技术工作场所使用过Nextflow，但没有详细说明其优缺点。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是不同工作流语言的选择及其优缺点，特别是对Groovy的不满和对Nextflow在HPC环境中的表现的讨论。
• 另一个值得注意的点是工作流语言在不同基础设施（如HPC和AWS）上的适应性和性能表现。
• 讨论还涉及到从一种语言或工具迁移到另一种语言或工具的学习曲线和潜在收益，如从Snakemake转向Nextflow是否值得。
• 工业应用中对工作流语言的选择和维护成本也被提及，特别是在跨团队和跨基础设施的情况下。

"Dataflow variables are spectacularly expressive in concurrent programming"
Henri E. Bal , Jennifer G. Steiner , Andrew S. Tanenbaum
Nextflow is a workflow system for creating scalable, portable, and reproducible workflows. It is based on the dataflow programming model, which greatly simplifies the writing of parallel and distributed pipelines, allowing you to focus on the flow of data and computation. Nextflow can deploy workflows on a variety of execution platforms, including your local machine, HPC schedulers, AWS Batch, Azure Batch, Google Cloud Batch, and Kubernetes. Additionally, it supports many ways to manage your software dependencies, including Conda, Spack, Docker, Podman, Singularity, and more.
Quick start
Install Nextflow with a single command:
curl -fsSL https://get.nextflow.io
|
bash
It creates the
nextflow
executable file in the current directory. You can then move it to a directory in your
$PATH
to run it from anywhere.
Nextflow can also be installed from Bioconda:
conda install -c bioconda nextflow
Documentation
The Nextflow documentation is available for the latest
stable
and
edge
releases.
Community
You can post questions and get help in the
Nextflow community forum
or the
Nextflow Slack
. Bugs and feature requests should be reported as
GitHub issues
.
The Nextflow community is highly active with regular community meetings, events, a podcast and more. You can view much of this material on the
Nextflow
and
nf-core
YouTube channels.
The
nf-core
project is a community effort aggregating high quality Nextflow workflows which can be used by everyone.
Contributing
Contributions are more than welcome. See the
CONTRIBUTING
file for details.
License
Nextflow is released under the Apache 2.0 license. Nextflow is a
registered trademark
.
Citations
If you use Nextflow in your work, please cite:
P. Di Tommaso, et al. Nextflow enables reproducible computational workflows. Nature Biotechnology 35, 316–319 (2017) doi:
10.1038/nbt.3820
Credits
Nextflow is built on two *great* open-source software projects,
Groovy
and
GPars
.
YourKit
is kindly supporting Nextflow with its fully-featured Java Profiler.

data.title: The reality of firearm suppressors vs. Hollywood
data.author: bookofjoe
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了枪械消音器的实际效果，澄清了电影如《约翰·威克》中对消音器的夸张描绘。作者指出，即使使用消音器，枪声依然非常响亮，仅能降低部分噪音，远不能达到完全静音的效果。文章详细解释了枪声的组成：机械声、音爆和枪口冲击波，并通过分贝对比表说明不同枪械的噪音水平。例如，AT4无后座力反坦克武器的噪音高达187分贝，而使用消音器后，.22步枪的噪音仍可达140分贝。文章还提到，消音器的主要优点是保护听力和减少枪口火焰，但其效果和使用范围有限，并非所有枪械都适用。最后，作者呼吁读者点赞、订阅并分享文章，以支持其内容创作。

主要讨论点： Hollywood 电影中枪械消音器的表现是否真实，以及与现实中枪械声音的差异。

不同观点：
• **[saltcured的观点]**：Hollywood 对声音的处理具有高度的风格化，音频再现的动态范围有限，导致声音效果并不追求真实。例如，电影中的低语在现实中不可能在嘈杂的剧院后排被听到。同时，电影中的声音效果已经成为一种符号化的代码，而非真实反映。比如，Hollywood 中的鞋、饮料、衣服和性行为的声音都与现实不符。此外，旧的音响系统也限制了真实声音的再现，枪声在电影中已经被“消音”处理以适应播放环境，这导致需要进一步简化声音以使其区别于其他声音。

• **[idrathernot的观点]**：作为枪械爱好者，基于实际体验，他提到在现实中使用消音器确实能显著降低枪声，虽然不如电影中那么安静，但消音器与高质量子弹结合使用时，能有效保护听力并使射击体验更舒适。他指出，消音后的枪声更低沉，且没有超音速弹药的刺耳声。

• **[tstrimple的观点]**：tstrimple 认为，枪械爱好者在不同场合对消音器的描述存在不一致。他们在对外时会强调消音器只是为了保护听力，而在内部讨论时却会夸耀能将枪械变得“Hollywood 安静”。此外，Hollywood 在表现消音武器时，最误导人的不仅是枪声本身，还有子弹撞击目标的声音，后者在现实中往往比枪声更响亮。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点**：Hollywood 对枪声的表现是否误导观众，以及现实中消音器的效果与电影中的差距。枪械爱好者之间对消音器效果的描述也存在不一致，部分人认为电影夸大了消音效果，而另一部分人则认为在特定条件下可以实现接近电影中的效果。

• **例子和论据**：
  - saltcured 提到了电影声音风格化和符号化的例子，以及 Dirty Harry 电影中对枪声的艺术化处理。
  - idrathernot 通过个人经验说明了消音器在现实中的效果，并提供了实际使用消音器的例子。
  - tstrimple 提供了 YouTube 视频链接以支持其观点，并指出了 Hollywood 在表现消音武器时子弹撞击声的误导性。

这些讨论展示了电影艺术化处理与现实体验之间的显著差异，以及枪械爱好者在不同语境下对消音器效果的不同描述。

44578181.article_content:
The reality of firearm suppressors.
June 12, 2025
16 minutes
Hello again. I’m going to stick on the topic of intermediate ballistics this week, but go into a bit more detail on silencers/suppressors
1
. I hinted last week that I might go on a deep dive, and I’ve had a few questions about silencers, so let’s strike while the iron (or gun barrel) is hot.
As this post’s title suggests, we’ll debunk the myth created by Hollywood that a firearm can be completely silenced, reduced only to a “pew”. I’ll pull together some examples of silenced firearms and show what silencers/suppressors can and can’t do, and compare the noises you’d get to some other types of sound. Then I’ll go into the components which make up firearm noise: mechanical, sonic boom, and muzzle blast. Then I’ll discuss the advantages that silencers bring, even though they’re not as impressive as they seem in the movies. Finally, I’ll sum up by discussing the limitations of silencers and why they are not universal.
I included this clip from
John Wick: Chapter 2
in last week’s post, but I didn’t give it the attention it deserved as a truly ridiculous piece of cinema. Really, it deserves its own post just
like I did with
The Expendables
, it’s that ridiculous, but instead we’ll use it as an anchor for today’s discussion while we also pull in some other Hollywood examples. Thankfully for us, there’s no shortage of unrealistic silencers on screen. Here’s the John Wick clip again:
This warrants another entry in the Realism vs. Drama Hall of Fame:
This is probably a bit on the generous side for John Wick, but he’s in exalted company. I often read about how realistic the “gunplay” in these movies is, as if that wasn’t an oxymoron. The director has the right idea:
it’s comic book action
.
One thing I won’t be silent about is my usual request for you to “like,” subscribe, and share this post if you’ve enjoyed it. There’s a handy subscription link below. It really helps. Please also comment below if you want to join in the conversation. Alternatively you can contact me via
webform here
or
email here
.
Type your email…
Subscribe
<< Bullets flying backwards
Send in the troops (Part 1) >>
Even a quieter gunshot is still very loud
Gunshots are very loud things, so even when you eliminate most of their noise, they’re still loud. Last week
I mentioned decibels
, which are the unit of measurement of sound intensity level (i.e. loudness). Here’s a chart (you can find any number
like this on Google
) which compares the decibel level of some common things:
Please take this with a grain of salt. Sounds vary depending on how close you are, and no distances are specified here.
Decibels are a funny unit, designed to measure the wide range of sound pressure levels that correspond to loudness. For example, 180 dB is a billion billion times louder than 0 dB
2
. I don’t know about you, but I can’t picture a billion billion anything. To make matters more complicated, our ears
don’t respond in a linear way
to sound pressure. It’s like they have their own algorithm in there to make sense of the world (your brain, I suppose). All you need to know is that:
An increase of 10 dB is ten times louder, but sounds twice as loud
A decrease of 10 dB is ten times quieter, but sounds half as loud
An increase of 3 dB is a doubling in loudness, but is the smallest increase in volume we can perceive
A decrease of 3 dB is a halving in loudness, but is the smallest decrease in volume we can perceive
We see that “explosion” tops out the scale in the chart above, at 150 dB. How does this compare with gunshots? The loudness of a weapon (or anything) depends on the strength of the pressure wave and how close the listener is to the source. The problem with the above chart is that there are no distances, but we do have
some firearms data
which is calibrated to an observer 1 m away from the gun:
Firing a…
…registers…
AT4
recoilless anti-tank weapon
187 dB (
according to this
source). Might be measured closer than 1 m.
Smith & Wesson 586
.357 Magnum pistol
169 dB
Remington 742
rifle (.30-06 calibre, standard 22″ barrel)
161.6 dB
Remington SP-10 10-gauge shotgun
161.4 dB
Glock 22
.40 pistol
159 dB
AR-15
5.56mm rifle
158.9 dB
.22 rifle
140 dB (no distance specified,
this source
).
For some context to these numbers, 187 dB feels 20 to 130 times louder than the pain threshold of hearing (115-140 dB). 160 dB feels more than twice as loud (and is actually more like 10x as loud) as the top of most decibel charts. 140 dB is the level above which
hearing protection is mandatory
in the workplace, no matter how short the exposure it.
So much for unsilenced firearms. What difference does a silencer make? Dakota Silencer (now known as
Silencer Central
) produced a handy graphic comparing the difference between unsuppressed and suppressed versions of common firearms
3

company link here
, but high-quality version of graphic
available here

44578181.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了枪械消音器的实际效果，澄清了电影如《约翰·威克》中对消音器的夸张描绘。作者指出，即使使用消音器，枪声依然非常响亮，仅能降低部分噪音，远不能达到完全静音的效果。文章详细解释了枪声的组成：机械声、音爆和枪口冲击波，并通过分贝对比表说明不同枪械的噪音水平。例如，AT4无后座力反坦克武器的噪音高达187分贝，而使用消音器后，.22步枪的噪音仍可达140分贝。文章还提到，消音器的主要优点是保护听力和减少枪口火焰，但其效果和使用范围有限，并非所有枪械都适用。最后，作者呼吁读者点赞、订阅并分享文章，以支持其内容创作。

data.title: Thunderbird: Fluent Windows 11 Design
data.author: skipnup
data.article_summary: FluentBird是一款为Mozilla Thunderbird设计的userChrome.css主题，实现了Windows 11的Fluent Design和Mica透明材质效果。该主题支持亮色和暗色模式，增强了Thunderbird在Windows 11系统上的视觉体验。最新版本0.1.5修复了暗模式下的信封图形问题，并解决了卡片视图中主题冲突等问题。安装需启用userChrome.css，并将相关文件复制到Thunderbird的配置目录中。由于是测试版，仍存在一些未完成的样式和已知问题，如无法完全主题化所有元素。该项目基于MIT许可证发布。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Thunderbird的界面设计及其自定义主题功能

不同观点：
• paintbox认为搜索栏占用太多空间，影响界面美观和空间利用，并希望借鉴浏览器设计演变的经验来改进。
• ttoinou则认为应用的默认设计往往是最适合长时间使用和减少眼部疲劳的，尽管不美观但有效，并以自己多年使用Thunderbird的经验为例。
• ape4澄清了对"fluent"设计名称的误解，指出它实际上是指微软的一种设计风格，而非编程中的流畅接口。
• huhtenberg批评设计中有太多空白空间，信息密度低，但认为这种设计可能会在设计社区中受欢迎。
• accrual欣赏"Fluent"设计的透明效果，并希望通过这种设计带回早期玻璃效果的美学，同时对搜索栏的位置有所保留。
• bluedino对现代屏幕只能显示少量邮件列表表示不满，怀念早期邮件客户端的设计。
• MortyWaves担心使用CSS而非操作系统原生实现可能导致问题，强调了原生实现的重要性。
• tummler对Thunderbird的整体性能提出批评，尤其是邮件数据下载问题，尽管喜欢主题设计。
• Calzifer提供了有关如何在Thunderbird中绕过Shadow DOM限制的技术细节，分享了个人经验和解决方案。
• AdmiralAsshat提到仍在使用一个多年未更新的Monterail主题，并对该主题的开发停滞表示遗憾。
• thesuitonym和guluarte都不理解为什么有人想把Thunderbird设计得像Outlook，表现出对这种设计趋势的困惑。
• hk1337惊讶Thunderbird仍在更新，并对跨平台使用Windows 11设计表示好奇。
• kookamamie担心Thunderbird是否仍然存在可能损坏邮件的bug，对软件稳定性提出质疑。
• neogodless希望看到更多有关多文件夹管理的界面截图，关注设计的实际应用效果。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及到Thunderbird的界面空间利用、信息密度、主题美观与实用性的平衡、Shadow DOM的技术问题以及对软件稳定性和性能的关注。
• 争议的焦点包括搜索栏的位置和空间使用、默认设计与自定义主题的优劣、以及设计是否应借鉴其他应用（如Outlook）等问题。
• 部分用户关注设计的实际效果和长期使用体验，而其他用户则更在意技术实现和软件功能。

FluentBird
FluentBird is a userChrome.css theme for Mozilla Thunderbird, that implemenets Windows 11 Fluent Design and Mica transparency materials.
Created by Danny King -
www.dannyking.co.uk
Released under the MIT License
Features
Implements Fluent Design styling in Thunderbird
Supports both dark and light modes (system theme)
Enhances and highlights Mica transparency on Windows 11 systems
This will likely be the last beta release, unless more issues are raised, with 1.0 release to occur alongside Thunderbird 141.
0.1.5 Release Notes
Improves the "no messages" envolope graphic in dark mode.
Fixes the subject line clashing with the star / tags icons in card view.
0.1.4 Release Notes
Adds Fluent icons and correct button styling for the "Reply List" button
Fixes button hover colour in Dark Mode
Fixes subject line colour on card view in Dark Mode
Credits
FluentBird uses Fluent Design icons provided by Microsoft, licensed under the MIT License.
Copyright (c) Microsoft Corporation.
Setup Instructions
Enable userChrome.css
Open Thunderbird
Go to
Settings
>
General
Click
Config Editor…
under
Advanced
Search for
toolkit.legacyUserProfileCustomizations.stylesheets
Set it to
true
Restart Thunderbird
Enable the Mica flags in Thunderbird’s (Firefox-based) advanced configuration:
Open Thunderbird
Go to
Settings
>
General
Scroll down and click
Config Editor…
under
Advanced
In the search bar, type
widget.windows.mica
and set it to
true
Search for
widget.windows.mica.popups
and set it to
2
Make sure no other theme is selected in Thunderbird settings.
Do not
select Light, Dark, or any theme from the Thunderbird extension store.
The theme must be set to "System Theme" or simply unselected.
Copy the included files to the
chrome
folder in your Thunderbird profile directory:
Click on Help > Troubleshooting information
Scroll down to "Profile Folder" under "Application Basics" and click "Open Folder"
Create a new folder named
chrome
inside your profile folder, if it does not already exist
Place the userChrome.css file and all folders into the 'chrome' directory
Restart Thunderbird.
Known Issues
This is a beta release. Expect bugs and incomplete styling.
Untested on Mac and Linux (should work, but without Mica).
Report issues via the GitHub repository.
Also, note that some areas of ThunderBird are rendered outside of the influence of userChrome.css in a "Shadow DOM" - as such, it is not possible to fully theme all elements of Thunderbird.
The mail section is fully themed, as is the general window chrome. The Contacts, Calendar, Tasks and Chat functions have limited themeing in some areas.
It isn't possible to style the new message / reply message window, or any other pop-up windows.
As they are entirely contained within a Shadow DOM, it is also not possible to theme the settings areas.
Questions?
Check the GitHub repo or open an issue there. Enjoy!

data.article_summary: 文章描述了作者在网络上看到糟糕新闻时的无力感，尽管与自己无关，但仍感到这些事不该发生。这种情境下，作者有种想立即做出反应的冲动，类似于想把报纸揉皱扔掉，但在屏幕上却无法表达不满。为此，作者开发了一个浏览器扩展程序，点击按钮后，网页会被一群像饥饿食人鱼般的光标慢慢撕碎。文章末尾提供了在Firefox和Chrome上安装的链接，并附带了一些相关的科技主题和订阅选项。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对“桌面玩具”类程序的回忆、联想及其背后的意义

不同观点：
• [reconnecting] 认为此类程序早在30年前就存在，称之为“桌面玩具”，并提供了一个1995年的例子作为论据，表明这类程序并非新概念。
• [waltbosz] 联想到一个名为 face.com 的早期DOS程序（1980年代末），描述了该程序如何在文本控制台上显示字符并与用户互动，提到了两个有趣的控制功能（聚集和跳舞），进一步佐证早期“玩具应用”的存在。
• [OneFriend2575] 认为这种程序表面上是愚蠢的乐趣，但具有更深层的意义，例如重新获得控制权和改变对网络内容的感受，指出这种互动可以影响用户对网络环境的情感反应。
• [jihadjihad] 以一种幽默的方式评论MrBeast被数字食人鱼吞噬，带有诗意的隐喻，可能暗示对名人或网络文化的某种看法。
• [Stevemiller07] 对“Pixel Piranhas”程序表现出兴趣，询问其是否为开源或仍在早期访问阶段，显示出对该程序技术状态的关注。
• [poulpy123] 以调侃的方式评论该程序比“打屏幕”更省钱，表现出对压力释放方式的幽默理解。

补充讨论：
• 该讨论中涉及到早期计算机程序的历史，特别是DOS时代的玩具应用，展示了这类程序的演变。
• 部分评论者如[OneFriend2575]深入探讨了这种程序的心理和情感影响，提出了对用户界面自定义的新视角。
• 争议的焦点可能在于这种程序的价值和意义，一些人认为其仅为娱乐，另一些人如[OneFriend2575]则看到了更深层次的象征意义。

44550967.article_content:
I really hate it when I’m  exposed to some horrible news online, and feel powerless. There is nothing I can do, I am not responsible, and yet at the same time I have this feeling “this shouldn’t be happening”.
There is a temptation to immediately react â if it was printed, I would crumple up the paper and throw it away â yet, reading pixels on the screen I don’t have the right gesture to express my discontent.
So I made this little browser extension. Click on a button, and a horde of cursors, like hungry piranhas, will slowly rip the web page apart for you.

data.title: MARS.EXE → COM (2021)
data.author: reconnecting
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了1993年由Tim J. Clarke编写的火星景观渲染器代码，对其进行了详细分析和研究。原始的MARS.EXE文件大小为5649字节，作者对其进行反汇编、重写和优化，将其压缩至1517字节。文章提供了原始代码和优化后的MARS.COM代码，并详细说明了转换过程和算法。此外，文章还介绍了如何使用DEBUG工具提取和解析二进制数据，同时提醒操作时需谨慎。作者尝试联系原作者Tim未果，希望他能看到此文并取得联系。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于经典DOS时代3D演示程序MARS.EXE及其技术实现的讨论

不同观点：
• **对MARS.EXE的赞美与怀旧**：
  - [skrebbel] 和 [reconnecting] 提到MARS.EXE作为经典DOS演示程序，在1993年时带来了极大的震撼，尤其是其实时渲染的分形地形效果在当时的硬件条件下显得不可思议。
  - [Andrew_nenakhov] 表示对MARS.EXE这一名字久违的怀念。

• **技术细节与实现方式**：
  - [reconnecting] 引用了pouet.net上的描述，指出MARS.EXE是由Elixir的Tim Clarke在1993年编写，并且由于其出色的表现，Tim被邀请到Lunacorp工作。同时建议在DOS模式下运行该程序以避免崩溃。
  - [phkahler] 提到自己曾在学校用Turbo Pascal在486电脑上实现过类似的程序。

• **对微优化与现代技术结合的讨论**：
  - [londons_explore] 认为这种微优化虽然能带来巨大的性能提升，但非常耗费人力，并提出如果AI能够实现这种优化，可能会带来软件性能的革命。
  - [flockonus] 希望看到通过WASM等技术在网页上运行类似演示。

• **硬件性能与现代环境的比较**：
  - [amiga386] 质疑在现代多GHz机器上通过DOSBox模拟运行MARS.EXE与原生386硬件上的表现差异。
  - [baal80spam] 对比了MARS.EXE和现代Windows 11上的记事本程序，指出后者占用的磁盘空间显著增加。

• **技术探索与实践**：
  - [nickdothutton] 回忆自己在1988年购买了一本关于分形的Springer Verlag书籍，并尝试在z80家用电脑上复现分形图形，但速度非常慢。
  - [tetris11] 提到寻找可以在网页上使用的DOSBox来加载ASM，但未找到合适的工具。

• **算法与技术影响的争议**：
  - [kragen] 提出MARS.EXE是否预见了Comanche游戏中的Voxel Space 3D渲染算法的问题，暗示可能存在技术上的关联或启发。

• **其他技术发现**：
  - [shmerl] 提到在二进制编辑器中修改颜色调色板的经历，发现改变一个字节就能从红色切换到绿色或蓝色。

补充讨论：
• 评论中多次提及MARS.EXE的技术实现及其在DOS时代的突破性，但也有人关注如何在现代技术环境下复现或改进这种经典演示程序，并探讨了微优化和AI技术的结合潜力。
• 争议焦点可能在于MARS.EXE是否对后来的3D渲染算法（如Voxel Space）产生了影响，这一问题引发了对技术传承和创新的讨论。

data.title: Show HN: Improving search ranking with chess Elo scores
data.author: ghita_
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕Elo和Bradley-Terry算法的应用、变体及其在不同场景下的使用讨论

不同观点：
• **支持Bradley-Terry算法的观点**：  
  - timhh认为Bradley-Terry算法简单且有效，尤其适合主观性强的比较任务，如评估头发的直度。
  - 该算法通过成对比较构建客观排名，解决了直接评估困难的问题。

• **区分Elo和Bradley-Terry算法的观点**：  
  - slybot指出Elo和Bradley-Terry是两种不同的排名系统，Elo使用逻辑斯蒂分数函数，而Bradley-Terry基于比率，二者在分数尺度和敏感性上不同。
  - slybot还提到Elo评级系统的各种变体（如MLE、Bayesian Elo等），这些变体尝试改进Elo的某些局限性。

• **Elo算法在其他领域的应用建议**：  
  - rjmunro建议将Elo风格的排名用于评估Uber rides和餐厅评价，通过成对比较代替传统评分。

• **Elo变体的讨论**：  
  - Alex3917提问为何不使用不假设结果分布的Elo变体，并提供了一个GitHub链接作为示例。

• **对成对比较方法的批评与替代建议**：  
  - fulmicoton指出成对比较方法忽略了排名位置的影响，建议参考LambdaMART方法。

• **Elo应用于搜索排名的讨论**：  
  - patrickhogan1提出在搜索排名中使用Elo风格的截断，以避免引用低排名来源，并讨论了当前方法的缺陷。

• **工具和实现的推荐**：  
  - scoresmoke分享了一个Elo和Bradley-Terry的快速实现工具。

data.title: Pgactive: Postgres active-active replication extension
data.author: ForHackernews
data.article_summary: **pgactive** 是一个 PostgreSQL 扩展，用于实现 **active-active（双活）数据库复制。这种复制方式允许多个数据库实例同时接受写入操作，并相互复制数据，适用于多区域高可用性、减少写入延迟、蓝绿部署等场景。与传统的 active-standby 模式不同，active-active 没有单一的数据来源，因此需要处理数据冲突和复制延迟等问题。该项目利用 PostgreSQL 的逻辑复制功能，并通过扩展增强其对双活复制的支持。项目基于 Apache-2.0 许可证，目前有 426 个星标和 19 个分支。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Postgres的分布式和高可用性解决方案，包括BDR、pglogical、pgActive等工具，以及如何设置高可用Postgres集群和冲突解决机制。

不同观点：
• eatonphil 解释了BDR和pglogical的发展历史，强调了开源和闭源版本的演变过程。BDR1是开源的，而BDR2是闭源重写但后来被放弃。pglogical也有多个版本，且有部分被合并到Postgres 10中。最终，BDR演变为PGD（Postgres Distributed），并由EDB发布了PGD v6。

• zknill 分析了pgActive的工作原理，指出它使用Postgres逻辑复制来共享实例之间的更改，并采用基于时间戳的“最后写入胜利”冲突解决机制。冲突的事务会被记录到特殊表中以便后续处理。

• mosselman 提出了设置高可用Postgres集群的挑战，特别是关于自动故障转移和节点恢复。他提到了patroni与etcd、haproxy的组合，但感觉部署复杂。同时，pgool似乎是一个更简化的选择，寻求其他建议。

• nico 提出了一个关于“本地可写”只读副本的问题，希望副本能从主数据库接收数据但保持本地更改不同步回主数据库。他目前的解决方案是通过脚本定期获取数据并恢复到本地数据库。

• everfrustrated 质疑AWS为何会开发pgActive，因为AWS的RDS和Aurora分别使用块复制和SAN复制，似乎没有使用pgActive的场景。

• dang 提供了一个相关链接，指出pgActive是PostgreSQL的Active-Active复制扩展。

• iotapi322 强烈不建议使用此类插件，除非非常了解其工作原理，认为这并不是提升性能或可扩展性的好方法。

• ahachete 强调“冲突解决”实际上是“通过丢弃已提交的数据来破坏持久性”，建议要么避免写冲突，要么使用真正的分布式数据库如Yugabyte。

• dangoodmanUT 指出该方案似乎是异步的，这对事务隔离是一个主要问题。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于pgActive等插件的可靠性和适用场景，部分用户认为这些工具复杂且风险高，不建议轻易使用。
• 关于高可用Postgres集群的设置，讨论了多种工具组合（如patroni、etcd、haproxy）和简化方案的需求。
• 冲突解决机制的有效性和数据持久性是另一个值得注意的讨论点，部分用户对现有的冲突解决方法持怀疑态度。
