44556997.article_content:
Caana, the central architectural complex at Caracol, Belize, uncovered by Diane and Arlen Chase in the 1980s
Archaeologists from the University of Houston working at Caracol in Belize, Central America have uncovered the tomb of Te K’ab Chaak, the first ruler of this ancient Maya city and the founder of its royal dynasty. Now in ruins, this metropolis was a major political player in Maya history, dominating the southern part of the Yucatan Peninsula from 560 through 680 AD before its abandonment by 900 AD.
The discovery is the first identifiable ruler’s tomb found in over four decades of work in Caracol, the largest Maya archaeological site in Belize and in the Maya lowlands.
Te K’ab Chaak, who acceded to the throne in 331 AD, was interred at the base of a royal family shrine with eleven pottery vessels, carved bone tubes, jadeite jewelry, a mosaic jadeite mask, Pacific spondylus shells, and other perishable materials. Pottery vessels in the chamber included a scene of a Maya ruler holding a spear and receiving offerings from supplicants in the form of deities. Another vessel portrays the image of Ek Chuah, Maya god of traders, surrounded by offerings. Four of the pottery vessels portray bound captives (similar vessels also appeared in two related burials). Two vessels supported lids with modeled handles of coatimundi (pisote) heads. The coatimundi, or tz’uutz’ in Maya, was used by subsequent Caracol rulers as part of their names.
Archaeologist Diane Chase in the recently excavated tomb
Maya pottery basal flange bowl with a coatimundi head
Four jadeite tubular beads showing live and dead spider monkeys
Archaeologists Arlen and Diane Chase will soon celebrate their 50th wedding anniversary.
A team led by husband and wife collaborators Arlen F. Chase and Diane Z. Chase of the University of Houston has been excavating at Caracol for more than 40 years; this field season was carried out in concert with Belize’s Institute of Archaeology and was supported by the Alphawood Foundation, the University of Houston, the Geraldine and Emory Ford Foundation, and the KHR Family Fund.
The Chases estimate that at the time of his burial the ruler was of advanced age and approximately 5’7” in height. He had no remaining teeth.
Their investigations at Caracol’s Northeast Acropolis show that Te K’ab Chaak’s tomb was the first of three major burials dating to about 350 AD, a time of early contact with the central Mexican city of Teotihuacan, some 1200 kilometers distant. By 300 AD, Teotihuacan was a huge city that traded throughout Central America.
“One question that has perplexed Maya archaeologists since the 1960s is whether a new political order was introduced to the Maya area by Mexicans from Teotihuacan,” said Diane Z. Chase, archaeologist and senior vice president for academic affairs and Provost at the University of Houston.
“Maya carved stone monuments, hieroglyphic dates, iconography, and archaeological data all suggest that widespread pan-Mesoamerican connections occurred after an event in 378 AD referred to as ‘entrada,’” said Diane Chase.
“Whether this event represented actual Teotihuacanos in the Maya area or Maya using central Mexican symbols is still debated. The Caracol archaeological data suggests that the situation was far more complicated,” she said.
A cremation placed in the center of Caracol’s Northeast Acropolis plaza, recovered in 2010 and placed after Te K’aab Chaak’s burial has been dated to AD 350 by radiocarbon analysis and included artifacts from central Mexico. It contained the remains of three individuals, as well as two large knives, six atlatl points, and fifteen pristine blades of green obsidian from Pachuca, Mexico (north of Teotihuacan); several pottery vessels also likely came from central Mexico. Additionally, a carved atlatl projectile tip, atypical for the Maya but typical for a Teotihuacan warrior, was included in the cremation.
The cremation itself and its placement in the center of a residential plaza are also more typical practices for a high-status Teotihuacano and do not accord with standard Maya burial practices. Based on other ceramics in this cremation, the main individual was likely a Caracol royal family member that had adopted central Mexican ritual practices. This individual may even have served as a royal Maya envoy who had lived at Teotihuacan and returned to Caracol.
A third burial — the tomb of a woman, also covered with hematite and containing four pottery vessels, a spondylus bead necklace, mirror fragments, and two Pacific spondylus shells — was recovered in the northern building of the same residential group in 2009 and is similarly dated.
The three burials interred in the Caracol Northeast Acropolis all cluster at AD 350, at least a generation before the previously recognized Teotihuacan presence in the Maya area. They demonstrate that early Maya rulers were fully enmeshed in Mesoamerican-wide contacts prior to the Teotihuacan entrada recorded on Maya monument[s].
“Both

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：FOSS4G（Free and Open Source Software for Geospatial）年度会议的讨论内容、参会体验以及会议视频资源的获取。

不同观点：
• [N_Lens] 对会议中关于AI控制机器人利用地理空间数据的讨论感兴趣，尤其是当前大量投资涌入的背景下。他认为如果人工智能、边缘计算和开放地理空间标准（FOSS4G的核心）继续融合发展，可能会出现大量的机器人代理在物理空间中活动。他举例说明这些机器人可能类似于“非常智能的送货无人机”，而非电影中的“终结者”形象。

• [admaiora] 分享了参加FOSS4G会议的个人经验，认为无论是否直接从事地理空间领域工作，参加会议都会有收获。他特别提到，即使只是网页开发者，了解一些如Leaflet等地理工具也是有价值的。

• [qwertox] 关注会议视频的获取，询问会议直播录像何时以及在哪里可以观看。

• [dabber21] 对所有直播流同时开始的情况表示惊讶，可能在观看体验上遇到了一些不便。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及的趋势包括大语言模型（LLMs）在空间推理方面的进步、边缘计算使得移动机器人的实时处理成为可能，以及开放地理空间标准在未来机器人广泛应用中的重要性。
• [N_Lens] 提到了当前技术趋势的融合可能带来的未来场景，引发对未来技术发展和应用的想象和讨论。

争议焦点：
• 目前没有明显的争议，但[N_Lens] 对AI控制机器人利用地理空间数据的未来设想可能引发不同的看法，特别是关于技术发展方向和潜在影响的乐观或悲观预期。

data.title: Retro gaming YouTuber Once Were Nerd sued and raided by the Italian government
data.author: BallsInIt
data.article_summary: 意大利YouTuber Once Were Nerd因展示和评测基于Android的游戏掌机而遭到警方调查，这些设备支持模拟老式游戏机，并预装了大量未经授权的游戏ROM。意大利财政卫队（Guardia di Finanza）没收了他超过30台掌机，并要求他提供与设备制造商的通信记录。尽管模拟软件本身不违法，但这些掌机预装的盗版游戏可能违反了意大利版权法第171条，最高可判三年监禁。设备制造商多在中国，利用法律灰色地带销售产品。此事件可能导致该YouTuber面临刑事指控并关闭频道。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：意大利根据版权法对YouTube创作者Once Were Nerd展开调查并可能判刑，引发了对版权执法过度、法律公平性以及更广泛的知识产权讨论的争议。

不同观点：
• **观点一：执法过度，案件无实际受害者**  
  [user_7832], [Tade0], [marcofiset]等认为，此案中的执法行为过于严苛，尤其是针对一个并未造成实际损害的“无受害者犯罪”。他们质疑，对一个20年历史的游戏机和游戏的版权保护是否需要如此严厉的刑法，且意大利的版权执法历史一向严格。参与讨论者认为，此类案件不应动用刑事手段，尤其不应涉及监禁。

• **观点二：版权保护应被认真对待，尤其是商业侵权**  
  [Chronoyes]认为，商业层面上的版权侵权行为不应被轻视。他指出，许多YouTube大频道在公开评测中使用盗版游戏，并与个人下载ROM的行为区分开来。他特别提到，本案中的创作者不仅评测设备，还涉嫌销售盗版设备，这种行为值得严肃处理。

• **观点三：法律不公，大公司与个人之间的执法不平等**  
  [elric], [awongh], [jmyeet]等人指出，现行法律对个人和小型创作者过于严苛，而对大公司（如使用LLM技术的公司）则相对宽松。他们认为，现行版权法和执法存在双重标准，尤其是大公司（如AI公司）能够规避法律责任，而个人创作者却可能因较轻微的违规行为面临严重的法律后果。

• **观点四：版权法的适用和自由表达的冲突**  
  [basfo], [xg15]等认为，购买和展示合法销售的产品（如中国产游戏机）属于自由表达的权利范畴。将此类行为定为犯罪是对自由表达的侵犯。他们质疑，如果要打击盗版，应该从源头上阻止这些设备进入市场，而非惩罚个人创作者。

补充讨论：
• **LLM技术与版权法的潜在冲突**  
  [awongh], [bgwalter]等人提到，LLM（如ChatGPT）在训练过程中使用受版权保护的材料，但这些技术公司却未受到类似严厉的执法，显示出现行法律在技术发展面前的滞后性和不公。

• **意大利执法机构的过度军事化**  
  [Tade0]特别提到，意大利使用 Guardia di Finanza（财政卫队）这种高度军事化的执法部门处理此类案件，显得过于夸张，常规警察足以应对。

• **对公司高管和个人执法的双重标准**  
  [amelius]提出，在隐私侵犯等案件中，公司高管并未受到类似的刑事处罚，显示出执法中的双重标准问题。

争议焦点：  
此次执法是否过度，以及现行版权法是否公平合理，尤其是在个人创作者与大公司之间存在明显的法律适用不公的情况下，是否需要进行版权法的改革。

There are countless Android-powered gaming handhelds, but they go beyond the usual slate of Android games by offering console emulation support. The problem is the
game ROMs
on these devices, which are not entirely legal. Italian YouTuber Once Were Nerd is learning how seriously some rightsholders are taking game piracy after agents from the country's Guardia di Finanza showed up to confiscate his consoles. He now says the investigation could lead to criminal charges and the end of his channel.
Once Were Nerd has produced YouTube content covering a plethora of gaming topics, including Android-based handheld game machines from the likes of Powkiddy and TrimUI. These devices usually run an older version of Android that has been heavily modified for gaming, featuring built-in emulation support for retro consoles like SNES, Nintendo 64, PlayStation Portable, GameCube, and more. They've become quite popular as the cost of mobile hardware has come down, making it possible to buy what is essentially an updated PSP or Game Boy Advance for $100 or less.
Recently, Once Were Nerd attracted the attention of Italy's Ministry of Economy and Finance, which is tasked with policing copyright in the country. In the video first spotted by
Android Authority
(which has an AI-generated English language track), the YouTuber explains that Guardia di Finanza appeared at his door in April with a search warrant.
Once Were Nerd explains his legal woes.
Agents accused the creator of promoting pirated copyrighted materials stemming from his coverage of Anbernic handheld game consoles. While emulation software is not illegal, a surprising number of these devices ship chock-full of pre-loaded ROMs—the channel showed multiple Sony and Nintendo games running on the device. Once Were Nerd is far from the only channel posting about these devices, though.
Officials seized more than 30 handheld consoles and demanded copies of Once Were Nerd's correspondence with the companies making these devices. Once Were Nerd says he has cooperated fully with investigators and contends that he has done nothing wrong.
Legal gray area
The firms making these handhelds all operate out of China, which is beyond the reach of Western copyright law. They still sell the devices internationally, sticking to vague language about the inclusion of game ROMs. For example, Anbernic offers bundles with microSD cards marked as "compatible 7000+ games." That makes this approach to revisiting retro games a legal gray area at the very least. Authorities believe Once Were Nerd's activities may still run afoul of Article 171 in Italy's copyright law, which allows for up to three years imprisonment for violations.
It is unclear who made the original complaint against the channel. Once Were Nerd has seen documents that cite copyrighted material from Nintendo and Sony, but Guardia di Finanza doesn't need to reveal that detail until the preliminary investigation is finished, and cases can be brought by the agency itself. Our money is on Nintendo, which is
particularly litigious
when it comes to defending its intellectual property. When the investigation is complete, the government will either file charges or dismiss the case. Current law also gives officials the power to shut down the Once Were Nerd channel while the investigation is ongoing.
Italy has a history of heavy-handed copyright enforcement—the country's Internet regulator recently
demanded that Google poison DNS
to block illegal streams of soccer. So it's not hard to believe investigators would pursue a case against someone who posts videos featuring pirated games on YouTube.

• **观点三：法律不公，大公司与个人之间的执法不平等**  
  [elric], [awongh], [jmyeet]等人指出，现行法律对个人和小型创作者过于严苛，而对大公司（如使用LLM技术的公司）则相对宽松。他们认为，现行版权法和执法存在双重标准，尤其是大公司（如AI公司）能够规避法律责任，而个人创作者却可能因较轻微的违规行为面临严重的法律后果。

• **观点四：版权法的适用和自由表达的冲突**  
  [basfo], [xg15]等认为，购买和展示合法销售的产品（如中国产游戏机）属于自由表达的权利范畴。将此类行为定为犯罪是对自由表达的侵犯。他们质疑，如果要打击盗版，应该从源头上阻止这些设备进入市场，而非惩罚个人创作者。

补充讨论：
• **LLM技术与版权法的潜在冲突**  
  [awongh], [bgwalter]等人提到，LLM（如ChatGPT）在训练过程中使用受版权保护的材料，但这些技术公司却未受到类似严厉的执法，显示出现行法律在技术发展面前的滞后性和不公。

• **意大利执法机构的过度军事化**  
  [Tade0]特别提到，意大利使用 Guardia di Finanza（财政卫队）这种高度军事化的执法部门处理此类案件，显得过于夸张，常规警察足以应对。

• **对公司高管和个人执法的双重标准**  
  [amelius]提出，在隐私侵犯等案件中，公司高管并未受到类似的刑事处罚，显示出执法中的双重标准问题。

争议焦点：  
此次执法是否过度，以及现行版权法是否公平合理，尤其是在个人创作者与大公司之间存在明显的法律适用不公的情况下，是否需要进行版权法的改革。

data.title: ESA’s Moonlight programme: Pioneering the path for lunar exploration (2024)
data.author: nullhole
data.article_summary:
ESA的Moonlight计划旨在建立欧洲首个专用于月球电信和导航服务的卫星 constellation，以支持未来400多项月球任务。该计划将实现如卫星导航、视频会议和文件共享等服务在月球上的无缝使用。Moonlight将由五颗卫星组成，其中一颗用于高数据率通信，四颗用于导航，通过三个地面站与地球连接，覆盖范围达40万公里。该项目优先覆盖月球南极，该地区因地形优势适合未来操作。

Moonlight的第一步是2026年发射的Lunar Pathfinder卫星，作为后续完整星座的先导。随后，Moonlight服务将逐步部署，计划在2028年底开始初步运行，2030年全面运行。ESA正与NASA和JAXA合作制定LunaNet标准，以确保兼容性，并计划在2029年进行首次月球导航互操作性测试。此外，ESA还在考虑未来的火星通信和导航基础设施（MARCONI），利用Moonlight的经验和技术。Moonlight的启动仪式在米兰国际宇航大会上举行，标志着欧洲在支持月球商业市场和国际合作方面迈出了关键一步。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：欧洲空间局（ESA）的月球项目及其相关技术应用

不同观点：
• [技术应用的直接效益] ragebol认为月球导航功能对于着陆器的精确定位非常有用，有助于解决地面传感雷达在着陆引导中锁定过晚的问题，并指出过去的着陆器往往只能通过轨道图像确认着陆点。

• [优先事项的质疑] jcfrei对当前优先事项提出质疑，认为ESA在考虑月球连接性之前，应先解决地球上的通信问题，尤其是推动IRIS2项目以确保欧洲拥有自主的卫星通信能力。同时提到IRIS2项目预算仍未完全批准，计划2029年才发射，存在一定的急迫性和担忧。

• [文学关联] delijati提到了Daniel Suarez的《Delta-V》或《Critical Mass》这本书，可能是通过科幻文学的角度来看待当前的月球探索项目，但未提出具体的技术或项目评价。

• [支持与赞赏] CharlesXY对ESA主导这一项目表示赞赏和惊喜，认为ESA在推动如此 ambitious 的项目方面表现出色，并对欧洲在太空探索中的领导地位表示认可。

• [长远影响] BigChemical强调了Moonlight项目的重要性，认为它可能成为关键的基础设施项目，使月球探索转变为长期可持续的开发，重点在于让月球变得“可用”而非仅仅插旗宣示主权。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是当前项目的优先级问题，特别是jcfrei提出的对IRIS2项目进展缓慢的担忧，与ESA在月球项目上的投入形成对比。
• 另一个讨论点是月球导航和通信系统的潜在长远影响，BigChemical特别指出这将改变月球探索的性质，使其从短期任务转变为长期基础设施建设。
• 文学参考（delijati）虽然未直接参与技术讨论，但可能暗示了通过科幻作品预见未来科技发展的一种视角。

44560390.article_content:
ESA
/
Applications
/
Connectivity and Secure Communications
Imagine a near future where services such as satellite navigation, video conferencing, and file sharing are as seamless on the Moon as they are on Earth.
That’s the vision of ESA’s Moonlight programme, which aims to establish Europe’s first-ever dedicated satellite constellation for telecommunication and navigation services for the Moon. With over 400 planned lunar missions by space agencies and private companies in the next two decades, this programme marks a significant step towards sustainable lunar exploration and the development of a lunar economy.
The Moonlight Lunar Communications and Navigation Services (LCNS) programme is a partnership project between ESA and an industry consortium led by space systems developer Telespazio, with support from the UK and Italian Space Agencies. The programme will enable precise, autonomous landings and surface mobility, while facilitating high-speed, low-latency communication and data transfer between Earth and the Moon. This infrastructure is essential for humanity's return to and long-term presence on the Moon, while enhancing efficiency and significantly reducing operational and user costs.
A satellite constellation for lunar navigation and connectivity
Moonlight will be a constellation of five lunar satellites (one for high data rate communications and four for navigation), launched into space and carried by space tug from Earth’s orbit to the Moon’s. The constellation will connect to Earth via three dedicated ground stations, creating a data network spanning up to 400 000 km.
The Moonlight LCNS satellites will be strategically positioned to prioritise coverage of the lunar south pole, an area suitable for future operations due to its advantageous terrain. This includes elevated areas or "peaks of eternal light" – ideal for solar power – and "craters of eternal darkness" containing polar ice – a potential source of water, oxygen and rocket fuel.
The first step in this ambitious programme is the Lunar Pathfinder, a communications relay satellite manufactured by Surrey Satellite Technology Ltd (SSTL) and set to begin operations in 2026. This pioneering spacecraft will serve as a precursor to the full LCNS constellation, providing commercial data relay services and testing existing Earth-orbiting navigation satellites for lunar use. Following the Lunar Pathfinder, Moonlight services will be gradually deployed, with initial operations by the end of 2028 and full operations by 2030.
Collaboration and future plans
ESA is working closely with NASA and JAXA on LunaNet, a new framework for lunar communication and navigation standards. LunaNet ensures compatibility with future lunar infrastructures and technologies, allowing our global customer base to benefit from the services for their own missions or deploy complementary technologies to enhance the network. Moonlight will comply with LunaNet’s standards and undergo the first-ever lunar navigation interoperability tests, scheduled for 2029.
In addition to other programmes, Moonlight will contribute to a multi-planetary future by supporting the testing of instruments and facilities in lunar conditions, helping us better understand their performance in environments other than Earth. Looking further ahead, ESA is taking early steps towards a Mars Communication and Navigation Infrastructure (MARCONI), leveraging the technologies and experiences gained from the Moonlight programme.
[From top-bottom, left-right] Alexander Gerst, ESA astronaut; Daniel Neuenschwander, ESA Director of Human and Robotic Exploration; Javier Benedicto, ESA Director of Navigation; Gabriele Pieralli, Telespazio Chief Executive Officer; Laurent Jaffart, ESA Director of Connectivity and Secure Communications
ESA officially commenced the Moonlight programme with a contract signing ceremony at the International Astronautical Congress (IAC) in Milan. The ceremony was attended by Laurent Jaffart, ESA Director of Connectivity and Secure Communications; Javier Benedicto, ESA Director of Navigation; Daniel Neuenschwander, ESA Director of Human and Robotic Exploration; and Gabriele Pieralli, Chief Executive Officer of Telespazio.
“ESA is taking the crucial step in supporting the future commercial lunar market, as well as ongoing and future lunar missions. We are extremely proud to be working with industry and Member States to ensure that our technological capabilities can support and foster cooperation on the Moon with our international partners,” said Josef Aschbacher, ESA Director General.
"This year saw the first commercial soft landing on the moon, and we expect there to be hundreds of new lunar missions launching over the next decade alone. With these missions will come increased demand for communications and navigation services which can be provided by commercial entities,” said Dr Paul Bate, Chief Executive of the UK Space Agency. “The growth of a commercial lunar economy can bring real benefits

data.title: The AI bubble today is bigger than the IT bubble in the 1990s
data.author: akyuu
data.article_summary: 本文由Apollo首席经济学家Torsten Sløk于2025年7月16日撰写，指出当前的AI泡沫比1990年代的IT泡沫更大。文章比较了标普500指数中市值前十的公司，发现如今这些公司的估值过高问题比1990年代更为严重。文章提醒，所述内容仅为截至2025年7月的观点，可能会随时变化，不构成投资建议，投资者应自行调查并咨询专业顾问。同时，Apollo不对这些信息的准确性和完整性做任何保证，也不承担任何责任。注意，文中包含的前瞻性陈述可能与实际结果不同。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI领域的现状、泡沫可能性及其未来发展

不同观点：
• JCM9：认为当前的AI热潮与.com泡沫类似，技术本身有价值，但许多相关企业的商业模式不可持续。许多AI公司将失败或被出售，技术本身会变得普遍但不会成为独立的盈利中心。
• sigmoid10：当人们讨论泡沫而利率下降时是投资的好时机。当前的AI热潮可能会继续，因为现金依然廉价，但这并不意味着可以 indefinitely 持续。
• lucidone：认为AI在日常工作中很有用，但并没有显著改变工作流程，只是取代了部分工具如Stackoverflow。
• EZ-E：承认AI有明确的应用场景，但反对在每个产品或服务中强行加入不合适的AI功能，认为这是泡沫所在。
• vincefutr23：指出任何结论都可以找到支持的图表数据，暗示对单个数据点不应过度解读。
• Havoc：认为大部分AI生态系统会像pets.com一样崩溃，但底层技术是有效的，少数公司会变得更强。
• HPsquared：认为整体经济泡沫化，AI热潮与此有关。
• itomato：提出早期优势在于获取一级ISP访问，而现在只是现金和数据中心容量问题。
• lvl155：认为当前情况与.com泡沫不同，市场没有出现类似的大规模投机行为。
• torginus：投资者可能对AI未来的不同发展路径有计划，无论AI是否变得超智能或仅限于现有水平，Nvidia可能在“卖铲子”中占据垄断地位。
• khurs：引用Gartner的HypeCycle，认为当前AI处于炒作周期中。
• rayiner：不认为AI被高估，认为LLM确实具有革命性，能完成如写论文等任务。
• orangebread：提出存在meta-bubble和normie-bubble，大公司追逐超智能，而普通人在过度使用AI。
• roflcopter69：不反对对AI的投资，但反感虚假承诺，指出AI在实际应用中仍存在不足。
• dcchambers：认为AI泡沫破裂时会比.com泡沫更严重，因为当前许多公司在没有产品的情况下估值过高。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于AI是否存在泡沫，以及当前的热潮是否可持续。部分评论者认为AI技术本身有价值，但商业模式或市场行为存在问题，而另一些人则认为AI过度炒作且存在虚假承诺。
• 讨论中也涉及对Nvidia等公司在AI领域垄断地位的看法，以及对AI在实际应用中的局限性和潜力的不同见解。

data.title: N8n vs. node-red, which to use for AI workloads
data.author: daniel-payne
data.article_summary:
本文对比了n8n和Node-RED两种工具，帮助用户根据需求选择适合的平台。主要观点如下：

- **n8n**：适合处理公共云服务数据，集成AI能力强，尤其是与LangGraph和LangSmith结合使用，但缺乏内置的用户界面（UI）进行数据可视化，通常需结合ObservableHQ实现。
  
- **Node-RED**：适合处理私有数据源，尤其是文件和传感器数据，拥有出色的可视化工具Dashboard 2。然而，在处理需要大量AI计算的任务时，Node-RED表现不足，通常需结合FlowiseAI使用。

此外，文章强调了AI伦理问题，指出由于LLM（大语言模型）的非确定性，记录和分析决策过程至关重要。

总结：n8n适合云服务和AI任务，Node-RED则在私有数据和可视化上表现更优，用户可根据具体需求选择。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Self-hosted（自托管）与云服务的比较

不同观点：
• adastra22认为，自托管和云服务是更大的区别因素。自托管意味着用户自己管理基础设施，拥有更高的控制权和隐私，但同时也增加了维护的复杂性和成本。
• 一部分评论者支持云服务，认为其优势在于便捷性、扩展性和由服务提供商提供的技术支持。这些评论者强调，云服务可以降低运营成本，并快速响应业务需求。
• 另一部分评论者则支持自托管方案，指出自托管可以避免供应商锁定，同时对数据有更高的控制权，特别适用于对数据隐私和安全有较高要求的情况。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于控制权和便捷性之间的权衡。支持自托管的评论者认为安全性和隐私更为重要，而支持云服务的评论者则强调运营效率和成本效益。
• 有评论者提到混合方案的可能性，即结合自托管和云服务的优点，根据具体需求选择合适的解决方案。
• 具体例子包括：自托管在合规性要求较高的行业（如金融和医疗）中更为常见，而云服务则在初创企业和快速发展的科技公司中受到青睐。

44592006.article_content:
n8n vs node-red
Daniel Payne
3 min read
·
1 day ago
--
Listen
Share
Which to use
Photo by
Stackie Jia
on
Unsplash
TLDR
Try both, but my personal opinion is:
n8n
if you are using
public
cloud services for your data. But you will need to use something else if you want to visualize your information, e.g.
ObservableHQ
.
node-red
if you are using
private
sources, especially file based data or sensor data. But you will need to use something else for AI intensive workloads, e.g.
FlowiseAI
.
Reasoning
There are only basically two purposes when creating commercial computer systems;
Improve decision making; by turning data into information.
and
Reduce Boredom; by spiking dopamine or releasing serotonin.
There is a third, produce regulatory data. But that’s very boring and you don’t want to read about that.
Decision Making
I don’t know very much about reducing boredom, so I will concentrate on how these two tools can improving decision making.
Both products are focused on turning data into information, and sometimes that information is a trigger for another system to do something. They both excel at this task, however each lack one main component that is needed for effective transformations.
n8n is missing a UI
In my experience you can’t just create a computer system and leave it to run. That way lies disaster, all systems need “baby sitting”. Even in transforming data, we need to see intermediate steps, progress information and summaries of results.
node-red
has
Dashboard 2
, an excellent visualization library built around vueifity and chartJS.
n8n
is missing this, so I use
ObservableHQ
as my go-to visualization solution, but it can be a bit of a kludge accessing live logs.
node-red is missing Antigenic AI
These days we need to use LLMs to transform data, as well as extracting insights.
node-red
does have some LLM nodes, but it is missing integration with
LangGraph
, the main tool that is used to create Antigenic workflows.
n8n
is fully integrated into this landscape, and has excellent nodes for Antigenic AI.
node-red
is missing this, so I use
Flowise AI
as my platform for doing all things Antigenic. But I use
node-red
to prepare my data and put it into storage systems that
Flowise
can use.
node-red
is good at ingesting data into relational databases, creating vectors (with it’s basic LLM nodes) for storage, and also processing data ready for ingestion into graph data-stores. The
Dashboard 2
visualization is very important in ensuring things don’t go wrong; bad data in = bad information out.
AI Ethics
If you are new to AI and just starting out, AI ethics wont mean much, but it is going to be very important once you start building commercial systems.
The issue with AI is that it is
LLMs are non-deterministic; that is each time you run something you might get a different answer.
When you make decisions based on AI, you should always record the data & process that lead to the decision, document and log everything, especially in production.
As time goes by you will need to analyse all the bad decisions your system has made, so that you can improve future performance. You might also have to compensate prior consumers if they are effected by bad decisions.
Both
n8n
and
node-red
have good tools to record to persistent storage. However self-hosted
n8n
has the advantage here, as it has integration with
LangSmith
, a tool for monitoring AI.

主要讨论点：Gary Kildall 回忆录《Computer Connections》及其相关的早期计算机历史人物的贡献和影响

不同观点：
• [BruceEel] 提到Gary Kildall的回忆录《Computer Connections》，并提供了一个链接供读者查阅。这表明对Kildall在计算机历史中角色的关注，并引导读者进一步了解相关内容。

• [EconomistFar] 对比了两位早期计算机领域的关键人物，一位是从车库创业起步的（暗指如乔布斯等创业者），另一位是在系统内推动创新的（可能指Kildall这样的学术和企业背景的创新者）。该评论强调了创新路径的多样性和影响力的不同表现形式，指出影响未必一开始就显而易见或轰动。

• [comrade1234] 的评论较为简短且具有幽默意味，提及历史人物巴巴罗萨（Barbarossa）/腓特烈一世，似乎是在开玩笑或表达对另一类历史人物的期待，与前两位评论者的严肃讨论形成对比，并未直接讨论回忆录或计算机历史。

补充讨论：
- [EconomistFar] 的评论提出了关于创新路径多样性的讨论，并通过对比两位计算机先驱的贡献，指出了不同形式的创新和影响力。
- [comrade1234] 的评论虽然偏离主题，但通过幽默方式引入了历史人物，增添了讨论的趣味性。
- 争议焦点：尽管评论中没有直接的争议，但[EconomistFar] 对不同创新路径的讨论可能隐含了对主流叙事中单一成功模式的质疑。

data.title: Gmail/Google starts disabling features unless you agree to data processing
data.author: diggan
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Google Workspace 数据处理和功能之间的关系，以及用户对数据使用和收费的争议

不同观点：
• doctaj 认为，Google 并非故意扣留功能，而是因为没有数据就无法提供某些功能，例如日历中的航班信息需要访问电子邮件数据。
• jsnell 指出，Google 并没有不受限制地使用数据，数据使用范围已经明确限定在 Workspace 应用内。他还提到，相关设置已经存在多年，并根据各地法律/法规在不同国家默认开启或关闭。
• kotaKat 抱怨，即使关闭了所有相关功能，Google 仍然会因“AI”功能提高 Workspace 计划的价格，认为这是不合理的收费。
• xnx 质疑那些抱怨新功能的人，认为提供可选择关闭新功能的选项反而招致抱怨，有些不合逻辑。
• bbstats 简单表示，描述中的数据只是 Google 请求访问的数据，并没有实质性问题。
• pavel_lishin 提到，早期的一个功能（邮件到日历自动化）一直有问题，因此他总是关闭该功能。
• jstummbillig 认为，如果不允许数据处理，那么相关功能不工作是可以理解的。
• knorker 强调，Google 是在请求数据处理权限以提供这些功能，如果不允许，这些功能就不应该存在。
• antisol 虽然认为情况不理想，但质疑在 2025 年仍然使用 Gmail 却不希望数据被收集的用户的选择。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于用户是否应该为了使用某些功能而必须允许 Google 处理其数据，以及 Google 是否在通过这些功能和数据使用上进行不合理的收费。
• 不同用户对功能和数据使用的优先级有不同的看法，一些用户更关注功能的可控性，而另一些用户则对数据隐私和费用增加表示不满。
• 讨论中还提到了法律和地域差异对功能默认设置的影响，以及用户对 AI 功能和自动化工具的复杂感受。

data.title: NINA: Rebuilding the original AIM, AOL Desktop, Yahoo and ICQ platforms
data.author: ecliptik
data.article_summary: 这篇文章宣布了一个项目，旨在重现昔日的即时通讯平台，如AOL Instant Messenger (AIM)、ICQ、Yahoo Messenger和经典AOL客户端。项目团队正在努力尽可能接近原版重建这些服务，并记录整个过程。目前，AIM和ICQ已可自由使用，其中ICQ仍在开发中；AOL 4.0和5.0的支持处于alpha阶段，仅对支持者开放；Yahoo Messenger已公开可用并与Escargot网络互通。文章还提到Q-Link（Commodore 64上的AOL前身）以及提供社交平台和社区支持，包括Discord、Reddit、论坛和Wiki。

data.title: The limits of our personal experience and the value of statistics
data.author: alphabetatango
data.article_summary: 文章指出，依赖个人经验了解世界是有限的，因为世界很大，而个人经验非常有限。即使我们每天与三个人交谈，一生也只能接触到0.001%的世界人口。因此，要全面了解世界，我们需要借助全球统计数据和其他媒体形式。个人互动虽然能拓展视野，但仍不足以覆盖广泛的世界。新闻媒体虽然帮助我们看到更远的地方，但其报道往往片面且偏向不寻常的事件，导致我们对世界的理解可能有偏差。文章强调，统计数据和多样化的媒体来源对于构建全面的世界观至关重要。
data.comments_summary: 暂无评论

44591884.article_content:
It’s tempting to believe that we can simply rely on personal experience to develop our understanding of the world. But that’s a mistake. The world is large, and we can experience only very little of it personally. To see what the world is like, we need to rely on other means: carefully-collected global statistics.
Of course, our personal interactions are part of what informs our worldview. We piece together a picture of the lives of others around us from our interactions with them. Every time we meet people and hear about their lives, we add one more perspective to our worldview. This is a great way to see the world and expand our understanding, I don’t want to suggest otherwise. But I want to remind ourselves how little we can learn about our society through personal interactions alone, and how valuable statistics are in helping us build the rest of the picture.
The horizon of our personal experience
How many people do you know personally?
Let’s take a broad definition of what it means to know someone and say that we include everyone you know by name. A study in the US asked how many people Americans know by name and found that the average person knows 611.
1
Let’s assume you are more social than the average American, and you know 800 people. In a world of 8 billion, this means that you know 0.00001% of the population. A 100,000th of a percent.
2
It’s hard to visualize how small a fraction this is. If this illustration was drawn to scale, then the blue rectangle – which represents the world population – would be as large as a sheet of printer paper, while the yellow square – which represents the number that a person knows – would have the diameter of a human hair.
3
This is why I’m very skeptical when people say things about “the world these days” based on what they hear from people they know.
We cannot see much of the world through our direct experience. The horizon of our personal experience is very narrow. For every person you know, there are ten million people you do not know.
And chances are that the people you know are quite similar to you, far from representative of the world — or your country — as a whole.
Download image
How wide can the horizon of our personal experience be?
Perhaps you think restricting the people you learn from to the number of people you know by name is too narrow. After all, you also learn from strangers you meet, even if you don’t get to know their names.
Let’s assume you are exceptionally good at this, and you have a conversation with three new people every single day of your life.
If you can keep this up for 73 years, you will get to know 80,000 people.
4
That’s more than a hundred times the number of people you’d know by name.
This is still a tiny fraction of the world. After a lifetime of speaking with people, you will have spoken to 0.001% of the world’s population. For every person you’ve had a conversation with, there are still 100,000 people you’ve never spoken to.
Drawn to scale, the orange square, which represents the number of people you could ever speak to, would be less than a millimeter (0.8mm) wide.
5
I am focusing on personal interaction as the most direct and in-depth way to learn about others, but they are not our only experience by which we learn about others. We also learn by seeing other peoples’ clothes, by seeing their houses, or by hearing others talk about their personal experiences. But while these experiences also help, they still don’t get us very far. The world is large, and even if you are exceptionally attentive and exceptionally good at making connections and speaking to people, it is simply impossible to see much of the world directly.
Download image
The fragmented perspective of the news media: some spotlights on particular people, but much of the world is left in darkness
The limits of our personal experience don’t reach far beyond ourselves. How can we know about the world if we want to see beyond this tight horizon?
In one way or another, we have to rely on the media. Whether it is television or radio, the newspaper or photography, books, podcasts, documentaries, research papers, statistical tables, or social media.
This fact is so obvious that it is easy to miss how important it is: everything you hear about anyone who is more than a few dozen meters away, you know through some form of media.
That’s why the media we choose to rely on is
so
important for our understanding of the world.
The news is the media that shapes our picture of the world more than any other. Today, it’s often intertwined with social media. It is valuable as it lets us see beyond our own tight horizon, but the view the news offers is a spotted and fragmented one.
The news reports on the unusual things that happen on a
particular
day, but the things that happen
every
day never get mentioned. This gives us a biased and incomplete picture of the world; we are inundated with detailed news
on terrorism
but hardly ever hear of

data.author: bertman

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：游戏理论及其在身份认同、误导信息、社会动态以及人工智能系统中的应用

不同观点：
• [like_any_other] 认为身份认同在游戏理论中被低估。他指出，现实世界中的互动并非单人游戏，团队和身份在策略中起关键作用。通过削弱对手的集体身份，同时保持自己的身份，可以获得战略优势。该评论还提到，玩家可能会放弃准确的信息来源，转而依赖提供情感回报但事实不准确的叙述，以获得身份认同和心理安慰。

• [photonthug] 认为评论仅提供了高度概括的视角，并呼吁对游戏理论进行更系统的研究，特别是在认识论游戏理论和社会媒体操纵领域。他强调了这些研究对理解现实世界动态和制定应对策略的重要性，并指出经典行为经济学的“理性人”假设在实际应用中存在局限性。此外，他还提到了游戏理论在管理和人工智能系统设计中的潜在应用，特别是在健康与不健康官僚体系的区分以及AI交互协议的理论属性分析方面。

补充讨论：
• [photonthug] 提到了一个名为MCMAS的模型检查工具，支持代理、环境、协议以及认识论要素，并询问其他类似的软件工具。他指出，尽管在机器人学和自动驾驶汽车研究中，信念和知识模型有时会被采用，但在更广泛的AI和ML领域，预先解决模糊性往往被忽视，因为某些群体受益于“零理论”和“尝试错误”的方法。

争议焦点：
• 身份认同在游戏理论中的重要性：[like_any_other] 强调身份认同在策略互动中的关键作用，而[photonthug] 更关注系统研究和工具的开发，并未直接涉及身份认同问题。这表明两者在讨论重点上存在分歧，前者关注心理和社会因素，后者则侧重技术分析和工具开发。

• 游戏理论的实际应用：[photonthug] 认为经典行为经济学的“理性人”假设在实际应用中有限，而[like_any_other] 则通过身份认同和误导信息的例子说明了现实世界中的复杂动态。这反映了在游戏理论实际应用范围上的不同看法。

data.title: Numbers from my recent job hunt
data.author: Shane325
data.article_summary: 作者分享了他在2025年找工作的经历和相关数据。他从1月份开始全职找工作，6月份收到并签署了一份高级软件工程师的offer，整个过程大约6个月，但实际密集找工作的时间为3到4个月。他提交了73份申请，收到48个回复，进入10次面试，最终拿到1个offer。作者强调，内推是非常有效的方式，直接申请往往效果不佳。他建议不要广撒网式地申请大量职位，而是要善于利用内推资源，多次挖掘个人网络。即使感觉内推用尽，也可以反复寻找新的机会。

• bix6 则对推荐是否真正有效提出了质疑，通过提问"在10次面试中，有多少是来自于推荐类别？"来挑战 willprice89 的观点，暗示推荐可能并没有其所说的那么有效。

• willprice89 的观点隐含着对求职者主动建立人脉的建议，强调了人脉网络在求职中的重要性。
• bix6 的评论则反映了对于推荐作用的怀疑态度，可能基于个人经验或对数据有效性的关注，显示出对人脉推荐效果的不同看法。
• 争议的焦点在于推荐在求职过程中到底有多大的实际作用，以及是否应将建立人脉作为求职的首要任务。

44589704.article_content:
Numbers from my recent job hunt
17 Jul, 2025
I recently started a new job as a Senior Software Engineer at
Headway
. Now that I'm a few weeks into my new gig I thought it might be fun to share some numbers from my job hunt.
I started job hunting full time in January 2025 and signed an offer in June 2025. A bit less than 6 months from start to finish. Although, I wasn't actively applying for jobs during all of that time so it's probably closer to 3 or 4 months of intensive job search stuff.
Here's the numbers at a high level:
Total applications submitted: 73
Responses received: 48
Interviews (not counting recruiter screens): 10
Offer stage: 3
Offers: 1
And here's a nice funnel graphic:
The above graphic is broken down by application type. My number one take away from this job hunt was
referrals are very powerful
and by far the most effective way to get to the interview rounds. I did apply directly to some roles but I quickly realized that that method was a waste of time and stopped. I cringe when I see people post on LinkedIn that they've submitted 800 applications and not heard back. Please don't do that. Unfortunately, the spray and pray method will not work in this job market.
A number of times I thought that I had tapped out my potential referrals, but ended up combing back through my network a 2nd, 3rd, or 4th time. I always ended up finding new referrals.
Feel free to contact me with any questions and I'll be happy to expand on any of the above numbers and offer some (maybe) helpful advice.

data.author: Anon84
data.article_summary: 文章主要介绍了一种由真菌驱动的新型生物混合机器人。该机器人由美国康奈尔大学和意大利佛罗伦萨大学的跨学科团队开发，利用可食用的帝王川菇（king trumpet mushroom）的电信号来移动和感知环境。这种真菌不仅帮助机器人移动，还能感知化学和生物信号，可能应用于农业等领域，如检测土壤化学成分以优化施肥。该研究发表在《Science Robotics》期刊上，标志着生物混合机器人技术的一个重大突破，因为真菌能够在恶劣环境中生长和生存。此前，类似的实验包括将人工虫脑放入乐高机器人和麻省理工学院开发的结合活体肌肉组织的机器。

Engineers have created a new type of
robot
that places living fungi behind the controls.
The
biohybrid robot
uses electrical signals from an edible type of mushroom called a king trumpet in order to move around and sense its environment.
Developed by an interdisciplinary team from Cornell University in the US and Florence University in Italy, the machine could herald a new era of living robotics.
“Living systems respond to touch, they respond to light, they respond to heat, they respond to even some unknowns, like signals,” said Anand Mishra, a research associate in the Organic Robotics Lab at Cornell.
“That’s why we think, OK, if you wanted to build future
robots
, how can they work in an unexpected environment? We can leverage these living systems, and any unknown input comes in, the robot will respond to that.”
Researchers from Cornell University in the US and the University of Florence in Italy placed a species of edible mushroom within a robot body
(
Robert Shepherd
)
Different inputs, such as ultraviolet light, resulted in different outcomes for the way the robot moved. A video of one of the mushroom-controlled robots shows it moving slowly across a surface by pumping its robotic legs. Another biohybrid robot uses a wheeled system in order to move around.
Combining this mobility with the fungi’s ability to sense chemical and biological signals could prove useful in a range of applications, according to the researchers.
“By growing mycelium into the electronics of a robot, we were able to allow the biohybrid machine to sense and respond to the environment,” said Rob Shepherd, a professor of mechanical and aerospace engineering at Cornell.
“The potential for future robots could be to sense soil chemistry in row crops and decide when to add more fertiliser, for example, perhaps mitigating downstream effects of agriculture like harmful algal blooms.”
Details of the biohybrid robot were published in the journal
Science Robotics
, in
a study
titled ‘Sensorimotor control of robots mediated by electro-physiological measurements of fungal mycelia’.
It is not the first time a living organism has been placed inside a robot body, though the use of mushrooms could offer a major breakthrough in the field of biohybrid robotics due to their ability to grow and survive in harsh conditions.
Previous experiments have included
an artificial worm brain placed inside a Lego robot
, which was able to recreate the creature’s movements and intentions.
Earlier this year, researchers from Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) created a machine that was integrated with living muscle tissue in order to sense and adapt to its environment.

data.title: LLM Daydreaming
data.author: nanfinitum
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了大型语言模型（LLM）在创新和发现能力上的缺失，特别是缺乏人类思维中的“默认模式网络”和持续学习能力。作者提出了一种“白日梦循环”（Day-Dreaming Loop, DDL）机制，通过后台进程不断从记忆中抽取概念对，并通过生成模型和批评模型探索和筛选有价值的联系，形成反馈循环，以产生新颖的想法。尽管这种过程成本高昂，但可能是创新的必要代价。文章还指出，LLM由于“冻结”状态而无法从经验中学习，并且缺乏持续思考的能力，这限制了它们产生重大突破的能力。最终，作者建议构建能够进行“浪费性”后台搜索的AI系统，以生成专有训练数据，从而绕过数据壁垒。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：大型语言模型（LLMs）是否带来了突破性进展，及其在创造力和新颖性方面的能力。

不同观点：
• 一些用户认为LLMs已经带来了实际的突破，但这些突破可能未被充分认可。例如，ashdksnndck指出，人们在使用LLMs得到好的结果时，往往不会特别注明这些想法来自模型，因为模型被视为一种工具，就像其他任何技术一样。
• HarHarVeryFunny和throwaway328则持相反观点，认为LLMs本质上是预测下一个词的语言模型，缺乏创造性和真正的突破能力。他们强调，LLMs的设计初衷是 recall（回忆）而非创造，因此期待其产生真正的创新是不现实的。
• zhangjunphy和OtherShrezzing指出，利用LLMs作为批评模型或进行创新研究的尝试往往不成功，因为这些模型在满足批评标准时表现不佳，且大规模应用也仅带来边际改进。

补充讨论：
• 关于如何评估LLMs的输出和新颖性，jumploops和A_D_E_P_T提到，识别独特见解需要高水平的专业知识和适当的提示。此外，LLMs在跨学科和新颖概念组合方面的能力有限，这也是其难以产生突破的原因之一。
• pilooch和sartak则探讨了结合不同算法和LLMs的可能性，认为通过搜索空间和进化算法等方法，可能在某些领域取得进展。
• 对于LLMs的批评和期望，velcrovan推荐阅读David Gelernter的著作，认为其探讨了创造性计算的可能性，而blueflow和cranium则对LLMs在数据评估和项目改进方面的表现提出质疑。

争议焦点：
• LLMs是否具备真正的创造力和产生突破性进展的潜力。
• 如何有效评估和利用LLMs的输出，以及在什么情况下LLMs能发挥最大作用。

整体来看，讨论围绕LLMs的能力和局限性展开，反映了对其潜力和现实应用的不同期望和看法。

Proposal & discussion of how default mode networks for LLMs are an example of missing capabilities for search and novelty in contemporary AI systems.

Missing Faculties
Continual Learning
Continual Thinking
Hypothesis: Day-Dreaming Loop
Day-Dreaming Loop
LLM Analogy
Obstacles and Open Questions
Implications
Despite impressive capabilities, large language models have yet to produce a genuine breakthrough. The puzzle is why.
A reason may be that they lack some fundamental aspects of human thought: they are frozen, unable to learn from experience, and they have no “default mode” for background processing, a source of spontaneous human insight.
To solve this, I propose a
day-dreaming loop (DDL)
: a background process that continuously samples pairs of concepts from memory. A generator model explores non-obvious links between them, and a critic model filters the results for genuinely valuable ideas. These discoveries are fed back into the system’s memory, creating a compounding feedback loop where new ideas themselves become seeds for future combinations.
The cost of this process—a “daydreaming tax”—would be substantial, given the low hit rate for truly novel connections. This expense, however, may be the necessary price for innovation. It would also create a moat against model distillation, as valuable insights emerge from the combinations no one would know to ask for.
The strategic implication is counterintuitive: to make AI cheaper and faster for end users, we might first need to build systems that spend most of their compute on this “wasteful” background search. This suggests a future where expensive, daydreaming AIs are used primarily to generate proprietary training data for the next generation of efficient models, offering a path around the looming data wall.
…I feel I am nibbling on the edges of this world when I am capable of getting what
Picasso
means when he says to me—perfectly straight-facedly—later of the enormous new mechanical brains or calculating machines:
“But they are useless. They can only give you answers.”
William Fifield
,
“Pablo Picasso—A Composite Interview”
(
1964
61ya
)
Dwarkesh Patel
asks why no
LLM
has (apparently) ever made a major breakthrough or unexpected insight, no matter how vast their knowledge or how high their benchmark scores. While those are, by definition, extremely rare, contemporary chatbot-style LLMs have now been used seriously by tens of millions of people since
ChatGPT
(November 2022), and it does seem like there ought to be at least
some
examples at this point. This is a genuine puzzle: when prompted with the right hints, these models can synthesize information in ways that feel tantalizingly close to true insight; the raw components of intelligence seem to be present; but… they don’t. What is missing?
It’s hard to say because there are so many differences between LLMs and human researchers.
Missing Faculties
Continual Learning
Frozen NNs are amnesiacs. One salient difference is that LLMs are ‘frozen’, and are not allowed to change; they don’t have to be, and could be trained on the fly (eg by the longstanding technique of
dynamic evaluation
), but they aren’t.
So perhaps that’s a reason they struggle to move beyond their initial guesses or obvious answers, and come up with truly novel insights—in a very real sense, LLMs are
unable to learn
. They are truly amnesiac. And there are no cases anywhere in human history, as far as I am aware, of any human with anterograde amnesia producing major novelties.
That may be an adequate answer all on its own: they are trapped in their prior knowledge, and cannot move far beyond their known knowledge; but by definition, all that is either known or almost known, and cannot be impressively novel.
Continual Thinking
But another notable difference is that human researchers
never stop thinking
. We are doing our continual learning on not just observations, but on our own thoughts—even when asleep, a human is still computing and processing. (This helps account for the shocking metabolic demands of
even a brain which is ‘doing nothing’
—it’s actually still doing a lot! As difficult as it may
feel
to think hard, from a biological perspective, it’s trivial.)
Research on science & creativity emphasizes the benefit of time & sleep in creating effects like the
incubation effect
, and some researchers have famously had sudden insights from dreams. And we have all had the experience of a thought erupting into consciousness,
whether it’s just an inane pun (“you can buy
kohl
at
Kohl’s
, LOL”)
, a clever retort
hours too late
, a
frustrating word
finally coming to mind, suddenly recalling anxious worries (“did I
really
turn off the stove?”) like
intrusive thoughts
, or, once in a lifetime, a brilliant idea. (Try meditating for the first time and writing down all the thoughts that pop up until they finally stop coming, and one may be amazed & frustrated!)

data.title: Voting age to be lowered to 16 in UK by next general election
data.author: hagbard_c
data.article_summary: 英国政府宣布，将在下次大选前把投票年龄降至16岁，以增加16和17岁青少年的公平性，许多人已经工作并可参军。苏格兰和威尔士已为此类选举做出改变。改革还包括放宽选民登记，允许使用银行卡和退伍军人卡作为选民ID，并打击外国干涉和非法政治捐款。新规将加强对政治捐款的审查，禁止外国资金影响选举，并对违规行为处以最高50万英镑的罚款。同时，改革还包括保护候选人免受骚扰和恐吓，禁止有此类行为的人未来参选。这些变化旨在增强选举透明度和公众对民主的信任。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：降低投票年龄至16岁的合理性及其潜在动机

不同观点：
• nonvibecoding认为，从理论上讲，将投票年龄降低到16岁有一定道理，因为许多16岁的青少年已经工作、纳税并承担实际责任。然而，他质疑政党支持这一改变的动机，认为政党可能只是为了获得选举优势。
• hunglee2持更激进的观点，主张投票权应完全普及，所有公民无论年龄大小都应拥有投票权。他认为，没有证据表明年长者的成熟度或智力一定更高，且较高的投票年龄并未带来更好的民主结果。因此，他主张民主应尽可能绝对化。

补充讨论：
• WalterGR没有提供实质性观点，仅指出该话题在其他平台上已有讨论，提供了一个相关链接（可能为重复内容）。
• 争议的焦点在于降低投票年龄的动机和效果。nonvibecoding质疑政党的动机，暗示其可能出于自身利益而非真正为了民主。hunglee2则从更广泛的民主绝对化角度出发，认为任何年龄的人都应有投票权，挑战传统上对年龄与成熟度的关联看法。

总结：评论主要围绕降低投票年龄的合理性及动机展开，有人质疑政党的动机，也有人主张投票权应绝对普及。

Electoral reform
Voting age to be lowered to 16 in UK by next general election
16- and 17-year-olds will be able to vote in all elections as part of changes including easier voter registration and crackdown on foreign interference
UK politics live – latest updates
Rowena Mason
Whitehall editor
Thu 17 Jul 2025 06.15 EDT
First published on Thu 17 Jul 2025 05.30 EDT
Share
The voting age will be lowered to 16 in the UK by the next general election in a major change of the democratic system.
The government said it was a reform to bring in more fairness for 16- and 17-year-olds, many of whom already work and are able to serve in the military. It brings the whole of the UK voting age to 16. Scotland and Wales have already made the change for Holyrood and Senedd elections, as well as local council elections.
In a sweeping package of changes, ministers will also extend voter ID to include bank and veterans’ cards to help more people exercise their democratic right.
As revealed by the Guardian, there will also be tougher new rules to guard against
foreign political interference
and abuse of candidates.
The move to extend the voting franchise fulfils a manifesto promise by
Labour
to give 16- and 17-year-olds the vote.
The package also appears to be taking steps towards encouraging more voter registration. Although it does not commit to entirely automatic voter registration, the government said it would move to an “increasingly automated voter registration system” that would reduce the need to fill out details across different government services on multiple occasions.
Angela Rayner, the deputy prime minister, said: “For too long public trust in our democracy has been damaged and faith in our institutions has been allowed to decline.
“We are taking action to break down barriers to participation that will ensure more people have the opportunity to engage in UK democracy, supporting our plan for change, and delivering on our manifesto commitment to give 16-year-olds the right to vote.
“We cannot take our democracy for granted, and by protecting our elections from abuse and boosting participation we will strengthen the foundations of our society for the future.”
The changes on election financing were welcomed by campaigners for transparency, but the new rules stop short of imposing caps on political donations.
Under the plans, ministers are to close loopholes that could allow foreign money to influence UK elections and there will be a crackdown on illegitimate donations through shell companies and new tests on political donors.
At the same time, there will also be stronger fines of up to £500,000 for those who break the rules, with any false or misleading declarations constituting a criminal offence.
Political parties will be required to assess companies they are receiving donations from against a series of tests, proving their connection to the UK or Ireland. Companies used for political donations will have to prove they are generating income in these countries.
Currently, any UK company can make donations to a political party, regardless of when it was set up, where its money comes from and who its owners are.
Some campaigners had called for more sweeping reforms after the US billionaire Elon Musk
floated the idea of giving $100m to Reform UK
– an idea he now appears to have dropped after tensions with the party’s leader, Nigel Farage.
He would not, as a foreign national, be able to donate under the new rules and would have to prove any donation through a UK-based company had UK-generated revenue.
There will also be enhanced “know your donor” checks, meaning parties will have to consider the risk of any money coming from illegitimate sources. New guidance will be provided by the
Electoral Commission
on conducting these risk assessments.
The committee on standards in public life and the Electoral Commission have previously called for strengthened regulations and greater transparency in political donations.
Another change is toughening the law to stop candidates, campaigners and electoral staff being intimidated, harassed or abused. Changes include no longer requiring candidates to publish their home addresses on election material, and changing legal guidance so that it will be considered an aggravating factor if someone is found guilty of harassing a candidate, campaigner or staff member.
Finally, the government is planning to change the law to ban those found guilty of intimidating or abusing a candidate from standing themselves as a candidate in future.

44591785.article_summary: 英国政府宣布，将在下次大选前把投票年龄降至16岁，以增加16和17岁青少年的公平性，许多人已经工作并可参军。苏格兰和威尔士已为此类选举做出改变。改革还包括放宽选民登记，允许使用银行卡和退伍军人卡作为选民ID，并打击外国干涉和非法政治捐款。新规将加强对政治捐款的审查，禁止外国资金影响选举，并对违规行为处以最高50万英镑的罚款。同时，改革还包括保护候选人免受骚扰和恐吓，禁止有此类行为的人未来参选。这些变化旨在增强选举透明度和公众对民主的信任。
44591785.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：降低投票年龄至16岁的合理性及其潜在动机

不同观点：
• nonvibecoding认为，从理论上讲，将投票年龄降低到16岁有一定道理，因为许多16岁的青少年已经工作、纳税并承担实际责任。然而，他质疑政党支持这一改变的动机，认为政党可能只是为了获得选举优势。
• hunglee2持更激进的观点，主张投票权应完全普及，所有公民无论年龄大小都应拥有投票权。他认为，没有证据表明年长者的成熟度或智力一定更高，且较高的投票年龄并未带来更好的民主结果。因此，他主张民主应尽可能绝对化。

补充讨论：
• WalterGR没有提供实质性观点，仅指出该话题在其他平台上已有讨论，提供了一个相关链接（可能为重复内容）。
• 争议的焦点在于降低投票年龄的动机和效果。nonvibecoding质疑政党的动机，暗示其可能出于自身利益而非真正为了民主。hunglee2则从更广泛的民主绝对化角度出发，认为任何年龄的人都应有投票权，挑战传统上对年龄与成熟度的关联看法。

总结：评论主要围绕降低投票年龄的合理性及动机展开，有人质疑政党的动机，也有人主张投票权应绝对普及。

data.author: mparramon
data.article_summary: 文章报道了大型语言模型（LLM）的性能正以每7个月翻倍的速度提升。根据预测，到2030年，LLM可能只需几小时就能完成目前一个月的工时。这种快速进展可能导致全球就业市场的剧变，并推动科技与科学的飞跃。作者Glenn Zorpette指出，这种指数级增长引发了对未来就业和社会影响的广泛讨论。

data.title: Claude for Financial Services
data.author: mildlyhostileux
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一种名为“Claude for Financial Services”的综合金融分析解决方案，旨在改变金融专业人士分析市场、进行研究和做出投资决策的方式。该方案统一金融数据，从市场信息到Databricks和Snowflake等平台的内部数据，整合到一个界面中，并提供直接链接以快速验证信息。方案包括Claude 4模型的领先金融能力，支持Excel任务和复杂分析如蒙特卡罗模拟和风险建模。它还提供预构建连接器，访问Box、Daloopa、FactSet、Morningstar等数据源。此外，方案确保数据保护，不会用于训练模型。多家咨询公司如Deloitte和KPMG提供实施支持，加速企业采用。Claude可用于尽职调查、市场研究、竞争基准测试、财务建模和投资备忘录生成等。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI在金融服务领域的应用及其潜在影响

不同观点：
• jasonthorsness认为，在信任Claude提供的投资建议之前，其自动售货机项目可能需要先取得成功。他还提出，金融和代码都依赖于小细节，但金融是否具有类似于代码的检查机制（如linting、编译、测试）来捕捉问题，这一点值得怀疑。

• injidup持怀疑态度，引用其父亲的观点，认为任何声称能帮助赢得赌场、赛马或股票交易的系统都是骗局，如果系统真的有效，就不会被出售。

• mildlyhostileux指出，Anthropic推出了“Claude for Financial Services”，新的模型在金融特定任务上表现更好，并与多种数据源集成。但金融业不同于纯文本工作，日常工具仍然是Excel和PowerPoint。他们质疑一个侧边聊天窗口是否足够，以及金融从业者是否会完全迁移到Claude上。

• hbcondo714提到，OpenAI也有针对金融服务的解决方案，表明Anthropic并非唯一涉足此领域的公司。

• gyosko警告说，“感觉投资”即将到来，可能会让很多人变穷。

• osn9363739认为，金融服务的范围很广，不仅仅是原始数据，还包括如何利用数据讲述想要的故事情节。他提到与四大的人交流，发现分析结果往往需要与客户反复讨论才能达成一致。

• dang引用了Hacker News的指南，指出提交的标题已被修改，强调标题不应误导或夸大。

• yodon呼应了“感觉投资”的主题。

• AdieuToLogic担心这可能会导致类似于2021年GameStop轧空事件的重演。

• asdev质疑Anthropic为何专注于垂直解决方案，而不是尝试成为所有人都能基于其构建的最佳水平平台。

• tom_m预测，初期可能会很痛苦，但最终可能会很酷，不过肯定会有人因此损失金钱。

• the_arun支持这一举措，并希望看到其他业务领域的特定服务。

• khurs指出，LLM在2022年推出，金融作为一个高利润且技术密集的行业已有2.5年的时间来推进。他询问现有的竞争情况，如JP Morgan的内部项目和Bloomberg的 offerings。

• eddythompson80认为，AI应被视为一种应用界面，改变的是交互方式，而不是功能本身。他举例说明AI如何简化财务分析工具的使用，无需学习复杂的软件操作。

• kaycebasques提到Bloomberg的模式，并询问其用户使用情况。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于AI在金融领域的应用是否可靠以及其潜在的负面影响，如“感觉投资”和市场操纵。
• 讨论还涉及金融服务的复杂性和AI如何融入现有的工作流程，特别是与Excel和PowerPoint等传统工具的竞争。
• 对Anthropic和OpenAI在金融服务领域竞争的关注，以及对垂直与水平解决方案的战略选择。

Product
Claude for Financial Services
Jul 15, 2025
●
5 min
read
Today, we're introducing a comprehensive solution for financial analysis that transforms how finance professionals analyze markets, conduct research, and make investment decisions with Claude.
The Financial Analysis Solution unifies your financial data—from market feeds to internal data stored in platforms like Databricks and Snowflake—into a single interface. Access your critical data sources with direct hyperlinks to source materials for instant verification, all in one platform with expanded capacity for demanding financial workloads.
Our Financial Analysis Solution includes:
Claude’s industry-leading financial capabilities:
Claude 4 models outperform other frontier models as research agents across financial tasks in Vals AI's Finance Agent
benchmark
. When deployed by FundamentalLabs to build an Excel agent, Claude Opus 4 passed 5 out of 7 levels of the Financial Modeling World Cup competition and scored 83% accuracy on complex excel tasks.
Claude Code and Claude for Enterprise with expanded usage limits
: Modernize trading systems, develop proprietary models, automate compliance, and run complex analyses including Monte Carlo simulations and risk modeling with Claude Code. With Claude, analysts can handle demanding all other workloads across critical market events and deal deadlines.
Pre-built MCP connectors:
Access financial data providers and enterprise platforms for comprehensive market data and private market intelligence.
Expert implementation support
: Tailored onboarding, training, and best practices for rapid value realization.
Financial institutions require the highest standards of data protection. By default, your data is not used for training our generative models, maintaining confidentiality of your intellectual property and client information.
The AI ecosystem for financial services
We've built the Financial Analysis Solution with leading financial and enterprise technology providers, giving Claude the ability to instantly check information across multiple sources. This creates a fundamentally more reliable way to analyze financial data—information is verified across sources to reduce errors, every claim links directly to its original source for transparency, and complex analysis that normally takes hours happens in minutes.
Through data providers, Claude has real-time access to comprehensive financial information including:
Box
enables secure document management and data room analysis
Daloopa
supplies high-quality fundamentals and KPIs from all public filings, disclosures and presentations
Databricks
offers unified analytics for big data and AI workloads
FactSet
provides comprehensive equity prices, fundamentals, and consensus estimates
Morningstar
contributes valuation data and research analytics
Palantir
builds AI-driven platforms that help governments and enterprises integrate, analyze, and act on large-scale data to make critical operational decisions
PitchBook
delivers industry-leading private capital market data and research, empowering users to source investment and fundraising opportunities, conduct due diligence and benchmark performance, faster and with greater confidence
S&P Global
enables access to Capital IQ Financials, earnings call transcripts, and more–essentially your entire research workflow
Snowflake
provides an easy, connected, and trusted data and AI platform that allows global enterprises to unlock value across all of their data – including structured, unstructured, and semi-structured
All of these integrations will be available today or in the coming weeks.
Accelerating enterprise adoption
Our ecosystem delivers both data access and implementation expertise through leading consultancies. These partners provide tailored solutions across compliance, research, and enterprise AI adoption:
Deloitte
enhances research productivity across equity research, private credit, and municipal bonds through their 10X Analyst
KPMG
helps financial services companies deploy AI assistants and agents to their developers and analysts
PwC
breaks down regulations into discrete obligations, analyzes internal compliance gaps, and generates policy updates through their Regulatory Pathfinder
Slalom
accelerates legacy code modernization through their AI Accelerated Engineering program, and provides solutions for end-to-end insurance operations transformation
TribeAI
helps investment teams automate deal material review, financial analysis, and entity resolution with VDR integration
Turing
offers auto-generation of compliance requirements in PRDs and Compliance Benchmarking-as-a-service
Use cases
Claude accelerates critical investment and analysis workflows including due diligence and market research, competitive benchmarking and portfolio deep dives, financial modeling with full audit trails, and generating institutional-quality investment memos and pitch decks. data.title: Cloudflare 1.1.1.1 Incident on July 14, 2025
data.author: nomaxx117
data.article_summary: 2025年7月14日，Cloudflare因服务拓扑更改导致1.1.1.1公共DNS解析服务中断62分钟，影响全球大多数用户，并造成Gateway DNS服务间歇性降级。中断原因是6月6日为未来数据本地化服务（DLS）准备时错误包含了1.1.1.1的配置，导致1.1.1.1的IP前缀被错误撤下。中断并非由于攻击或BGP劫持。事件从21:48开始，21:52时1.1.1.1的DNS流量开始下降，22:01检测到问题，22:54恢复。Cloudflare对此致歉并采取措施防止类似事件再次发生。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Cloudflare 1.1.1.1 DNS 服务中断事件的影响及技术问题分析

不同观点：
• v5v3 提出疑问，为什么用户在主 DNS 服务器 1.1.1.1 失效时没有自动切换到备份 DNS 服务器，质疑配置中的第二个 DNS 服务器为何没有生效。
• chrismorgan 对 Cloudflare 内部监控系统在事件发生后超过五分钟才检测到问题表示惊讶，并好奇为何警报系统没有及时触发。
• kachapopopow 指出 Cloudflare 频繁出现类似问题，而 Google 的 DNS 服务（8.8.8.8 和 8.8.4.4）在过去近十年几乎没有宕机，暗示 Cloudflare 在基础设施稳定性方面可能存在不足。
• jallmann 提到自己受到了影响，尽管已配置 Cloudflare 的 DoH（DNS-over-HTTPS），但仍遇到了解析问题，最终通过将 DNS 改为 8.8.8.8 解决了问题。
• homebrewer 建议使用 dnsmasq 设置多个 DNS 服务器并进行竞争响应，认为这样可以避免单个服务中断导致的问题。
• i_niks_86 指出许多用户假设 DNS 提供商之间存在故障转移机制，但实际上，操作系统或路由器级别的 DNS 客户端很少实现健壮的 DoH 故障转移，用户容易因此被困在无法解析的状态。
• CuteDepravity 建议在 1.1.1.1 出现问题时切换到其他提供商（如 8.8.8.8 或 9.9.9.9）作为备份，并对同时影响 1.1.1.1 和 1.0.0.1 的情况表示惊讶。
• perlgeek 从 SLO（服务级别目标）角度分析此次中断，指出此次中断可能导致 Cloudflare 服务降级至 99.9% 以下的可用性，并讨论了用户可能因此获得的赔偿。
• Mindless2112 提到自己使用了同时配置 Cloudflare 和 Google DNS 的工具，因此未受影响，并指出 DoH 未完全受到影响。
• aftbit 对多位工程师审核后仍未发现路由配置错误表示惊讶，并建议对 1.1.1.1/32 和 1.0.0.1/32 等关键 IP 进行特殊保护以避免类似问题。
• alyandon 根据自己的监测数据指出，Cloudflare 的中断时间可能比官方声明更长，质疑其声明的时间范围。
• cadamsdotcom 对 Cloudflare 的技术写作和事件处理表示赞赏，认为其声明透明且负责，展示了公司对问题的重视。
• chrisgeleven 反思自己过于依赖单一 DNS 提供商，建议设置不依赖上游解析服务的 DNS 服务器（如 Unbound），以提高网络稳定性。
• neurostimulant 提到自己的 ISP 会劫持 UDP 53 端口的流量并重定向到其 DNS 服务器，因此未受此次中断影响，但暗示这种行为是出于政府审查的目的。
• wreckage645 认为 Cloudflare 频繁出现全球性中断，显示其变更管理流程存在问题，建议对问题管理进行集中化处理，而不是每个团队各自为战。

补充讨论：
• 讨论的焦点主要集中在 DNS 服务中断的影响、故障转移机制的缺失、Cloudflare 内部监控和响应的延迟、以及对类似问题的长期解决方案（如多 DNS 配置或自建解析服务）的建议。
• 部分用户质疑 Cloudflare 基础设施的健壮性，并建议用户使用多个 DNS 服务商以减少类似事件的影响。

44578490.article_content:
Cloudflare 1.1.1.1 incident on July 14, 2025
2025-07-15
Ash Pallarito
Joe Abley
8 min read
On 14 July 2025, Cloudflare made a change to our service topologies that caused an outage for 1.1.1.1 on the edge, resulting in downtime for 62 minutes for customers using the 1.1.1.1 public DNS Resolver as well as intermittent degradation of service for Gateway DNS.
Cloudflare's 1.1.1.1 Resolver service became unavailable to the Internet starting at 21:52 UTC and ending at 22:54 UTC. The majority of 1.1.1.1 users globally were affected. For many users, not being able to resolve names using the 1.1.1.1 Resolver meant that basically all Internet services were unavailable. This outage can be observed on
Cloudflare Radar
.
The outage occurred because of a misconfiguration of legacy systems used to maintain the infrastructure that advertises Cloudflareâs IP addresses to the Internet.
This was a global outage. During the outage, Cloudflare's 1.1.1.1 Resolver was unavailable worldwide.
Weâre very sorry for this outage. The root cause was an internal configuration error and
not
the result of an attack or a
BGP hijack
. In this blog, weâre going to talk about what the failure was, why it occurred, and what weâre doing to make sure this doesnât happen again.
Background
Cloudflare
introduced
the
1.1.1.1
public DNS Resolver service in 2018. Since the announcement, 1.1.1.1 has become one of the most popular DNS Resolver IP addresses and it is free for anyone to use.
Almost all of Cloudflare's services are made available to the Internet using a routing method known as
anycast
, a well-known technique intended to allow traffic for popular services to be served in many different locations across the Internet, increasing capacity and performance. This is the best way to ensure we can globally manage our traffic, but also means that problems with the advertisement of this address space can result in a global outage.Â Â Â
Cloudflare announces these anycast routes to the Internet in order for traffic to those addresses to be delivered to a Cloudflare data center, providing services from many different places. Most Cloudflare services are provided globally, like the 1.1.1.1 public DNS Resolver, but a subset of services are specifically constrained to particular regions.Â
These services are part of our
Data Localization Suite
(DLS), which allows customers to configure Cloudflare in a variety of ways to meet their compliance needs across different countries and regions. One of the ways in which Cloudflare manages these different requirements is to make sure the right service's IP addresses are Internet-reachable only where they need to be, so your traffic is handled correctly worldwide. A particular service has a matching "service topology" â that is, traffic for a service should be routed only to a
particular set of locations
.
On June 6, during a release to prepare a service topology for a future DLS service, a configuration error was introduced: the prefixes associated with the 1.1.1.1 Resolver service were inadvertently included alongside the prefixes that were intended for the new DLS service. This configuration error sat dormant in the production network as the new DLS service was not yet in use,Â  but it set the stage for the outage on July 14. Since there was no immediate change to the production network there was no end-user impact, and because there was no impact, no alerts were fired.
Incident Timeline
Time (UTC)
Event
2025-06-06 17:38
ISSUE INTRODUCED - NO IMPACT
A configuration change was made for a DLS service that was not yet in production. This configuration change accidentally included a reference to the 1.1.1.1 Resolver service and, by extension, the prefixes associated with the 1.1.1.1 Resolver service.
This change did not result in a change of network configuration, and so routing for the 1.1.1.1 Resolver was not affected.
Since there was no change in traffic, no alerts fired, but the misconfiguration lay dormant for a future release.Â
2025-07-14 21:48
IMPACT START
A configuration change was made for the same DLS service. The change attached a test location to the non-production service; this location itself was not live, but the change triggered a refresh of network configuration globally.
Due to the earlier configuration error linking the 1.1.1.1 Resolver's IP addresses to our non-production service, those 1.1.1.1 IPs were inadvertently included when we changed how the non-production service was set up.
The 1.1.1.1 Resolver prefixes started to be withdrawn from production Cloudflare data centers globally.
2025-07-14 21:52
DNS traffic to 1.1.1.1 Resolver service begins to drop globally
2025-07-14 21:54
Related, non-causal event: BGP origin hijack of 1.1.1.0/24 exposed by withdrawal of routes from Cloudflare. This
was not
a cause of the service failure, but an unrelated issue that was suddenly visible as that prefix was withdrawn by Cloudflare.Â
2025-07-14 22:01
IMPACT DETECTED
Internal service health alerts
44578490.article_summary: 2025年7月14日，Cloudflare因服务拓扑更改导致1.1.1.1公共DNS解析服务中断62分钟，影响全球大多数用户，并造成Gateway DNS服务间歇性降级。中断原因是6月6日为未来数据本地化服务（DLS）准备时错误包含了1.1.1.1的配置，导致1.1.1.1的IP前缀被错误撤下。中断并非由于攻击或BGP劫持。事件从21:48开始，21:52时1.1.1.1的DNS流量开始下降，22:01检测到问题，22:54恢复。Cloudflare对此致歉并采取措施防止类似事件再次发生。

data.author: hhs

44591622.article_content:
Jul 14, 2025
Economists made a model of the U.S. economy. Our debt crashed the model
Under current debt projections, economists cannot even model out a functioning long-term economy.
National Debt
by
Stacey Vanek Smith
Play
Listen Now
Save
Share
Download
“We cannot even model out a functioning long-term economy under current debt projections," said Jessica Riedl, an economist with the Manhattan Institute who studies the federal budget.
Kent Nishimura/Getty Images
People have been worrying about U.S. debt basically ever since there even was a U.S. “The accumulation of debts is a most fearful evil,”
Thomas Jefferson wrote in 1787
. At the time, U.S. debt was around
$40 million
. Today, it’s closer to
$40 trillion
. At the same time, the U.S. economy is bigger and more powerful than Jefferson could have ever imagined, and things are looking pretty good: unemployment is near record lows, inflation is under control… so what’s the problem?
“Part of the problem is it's been this kind of ‘boy who cries wolf’ type thing, and people just get tired of it,” says Kent Smetters, an economist at Wharton, who has been crying wolf about the debt for years. He started to wonder: What exactly happens if the U.S. just doesn’t deal with its debt? He got a few economists and mathematicians together to build a computer model of the economy to play out scenarios.
They made a model of the entire U.S. economy, which required a lot of computing power. “This math problem was a big one,” Smetters said. “And the model computations are about 20,000 times bigger than our standard model.”
Smetters borrowed some computing help from Amazon and NASA and then he and his colleagues then fed the entire U.S. economy in all of its complicated glory into this mega-model. And the U.S. economy… could not compute.
“Their economic models crashed when trying to project out the economy over the long term,” said Jessica Riedl, an economist with the Manhattan Institute who studies the budget. “We cannot even model out a functioning long-term economy under current debt projections.”
The crash itself: not super cinematic, said Smetters. No flashing red letters, no skull and crossbones, no lightning bolt, just a few words that make a macroeconomist’s blood run cold:
Model not converging.
“The model's trying to find what's called a fixed point where everything just adds up, everything's consistent, and it's not able to do that,” Smetters explained.
In other words, if the debt keeps rising at its current rate and we just do not deal with it, even thousands of NASA and Amazon computers all working together cannot get the math to math.
“Really, it's a question of how far can we go before the bond market says, ‘I just don't believe that you're gonna pay us back,’” explained Smetters.
Bonds are like little loans. And the U.S. government sells billions of dollars worth of bonds every week. The interest rate it pays on those loans? Super low. Because people know the U.S. is good for the money.
If this were “The Simpsons,” the U.S. would be like Mr. Burns taking out a loan. The bank would very likely give him a really good interest rate: he’s rich, he’s got a great job, he’s got a big house. The bank could feel pretty sure it’s not going to lose its money.
Homer Simpson on the other hand, with his credit card debt, modest income, and some (donut related) impulse control issues would probably have to pay a much higher interest rate for the same loan.
Economist Jessica Riedl said the U.S. might be entering its Homer Simpson era. The country’s got so much debt that’s it’s outpaced what the economy earns.
“
The debt is projected to go from $30 trillion to $200 trillion over the next 30 years,” said Riedl. “That will cause interest rates to rise. Within a decade, interest is going to be one third of all of your taxes, and in a couple decades, interest could be 80% of your taxes.”
If most of the country’s money is going to paying interest on the debt, it can’t be invested into growing the economy, or filling potholes, or improving schools. It’s just going to pay interest. In cases like that, an economy will typically start to shrink: Services shut down, things stop working, businesses stop growing, they start laying people off.
So how long do we have before this happens? According to Kent Smetters’ model, about 20 years.
”The good news is we can actually make decisions now today that actually would stabilize the amount of debt relative to the size of the economy,” said Smetters.
Smetters and his colleagues published a
list of suggested reforms
that they think could help to fix the budget: raise the retirement age to 70, add a carbon tax, reduce social security benefits.
The chances of the government doing all of that? Smetters put it at about 5%. Not great, he said, but still better than the odds of our current path working out, which Smetters put at 0%.

data.title: Plasma Bigscreen rises from the dead with a better UI
data.author: bundie
data.article_summary: KDE项目Plasma Bigscreen正在复兴。该项目是一个用于电视的Plasma界面，最初支持现已停止运营的Mycroft AI助手。由于长期未更新，大多数发行版已放弃该项目，且在Plasma 6转型期间未及时移植。现在，Plasma Mobile贡献者Devin决定花时间对其进行全面改造。他清理了代码库，重新设计了界面，去除了面板背景，增加了背景模糊效果，并引入了搜索功能以快速查找和启动应用。设置应用也经过重新设计，采用双窗格布局，并修复和更新了多个模块。目前，该项目仍在开发中，计划在未来纳入官方Plasma发布计划，可能在6.5版本中实现。用户可以在Raspberry Pi上通过postmarketOS测试该项目。

44573752.article_content:
Lately, some KDE projects have seen a revival, like
Karton (the native virtual machine manager for KDE)
and the
improved ISO Image Writer.
Now, another abandoned KDE project, Plasma Bigscreen, is looking to return from the dead after long-time Plasma Mobile contributor Devin decided to spend a week overhauling the thing.
If you have not heard of it,
Plasma Bigscreen
is a Plasma shell for televisions, with original support for the now-defunct Mycroft AI assistant. It used to provide a simple launcher for apps and custom "Mycroft Skills" before development stalled, causing most distributions to drop it.
The project was left behind during the big transition to Plasma 6 last year because no one had ported it in time for the megarelease. After a friend of his started poking at the code,
Devin stepped in
to tackle the much-needed work.
He started by cleaning up the repository and then jumped into redesigning the interface, drawing inspiration from older Breeze mockups. The homescreen has been flattened, removing panel backgrounds. Here's a before-and-after comparison (click to enlarge):
One of the more visible changes is that the UI now has a background blur when you are navigating menus, giving focus to the foreground elements.
For actually finding what you want to run, you are no longer stuck scrolling through a long list, as Devin added a new search view, searching using KRunner to quickly find and launch applications.
The Settings application also got a complete redesign, adopting a simple two-pane look with a sidebar for categories. A lot of the settings modules (KCM) used hardcoded layouts, so Devin built a small component library for TV-focused UIs and ported everything over.
The rewritten Display KCM now uses the libkscreen backend, and the Wi-Fi and KDE Connect modules have been fixed and updated. Startup feedback for launching applications was also broken, and when you start up an application, a small animation now plays, similar to the one on Plasma Mobile.
For anyone who wants to test this out, you can do as Devin did by installing Plasma Bigscreen on a Raspberry Pi using postmarketOS, though you would have to compile it yourself or pull from the nightly repos to get the latest changes.
Applications like Kodi and
VacuumTube (smart TV version of YouTube)
work well with remote navigation, and some games like
SuperTuxKart
are playable.
Controller support exists, but getting TV remotes to work over HDMI CEC is still untested. The project is far from finished; it still needs an arrow-navigable virtual keyboard and a clearer long-term direction now that Mycroft is gone. Still, the goal is to get it back into the official Plasma release schedule, possibly for version 6.5.

data.title: New battery has life so long you may never have to recharge
data.author: Bluestein
data.article_summary: 韩国大邱庆北科学技术院（DGIST）的Su-Il In教授领导的研究团队开发了一种新型核电池——钙钛矿贝塔伏特电池（PBC），可为小型设备供电数十年而无需充电。该电池使用碳-14（放射性碳）和钙钛矿材料，结合量子点和双重氯基添加剂，增强了能量转换效率和长期稳定性。通过将碳-14应用于电极，并利用二氧化钛和钌基染料增强电子反应，电池的能量转换效率从0.48%提升至2.86%。尽管输出仍低于锂离子电池，但该技术被认为在生物安全性、耐用性和环保性方面具有优势，未来可应用于心脏起搏器、太空探测器和无人机等领域。研究团队计划加速商业化并进一步提升电池性能。

• 技术细节的透明性与可实现性：如电池的具体电压、电流及工作原理等是否能满足实际应用需求。

44591585.article_content:
Image by ThisIsEngineering via
Pexels
A research group at the Daegu Gyeongbuk Institute of Science and Technology (DGIST), led by Professor Su-Il In, has developed a new type of nuclear battery called a perovskite betavoltaic cell (PBC), which could power small devices for decades without the need for recharging. The team used carbon-14—an unstable form of carbon known as radiocarbon—and combined it with perovskite materials to create a hybrid battery with improved energy conversion and long-term stability.
The new battery uses radioactive carbon-14 nanoparticles and quantum dots (14CNP/CQD) as electrodes. These were embedded into the device along with a perovskite film treated with dual chlorine-based additives: methylammonium chloride (MACl) and cesium chloride (CsCl). These additives helped strengthen the crystal structure of the perovskite, making it more stable and better at moving electric charges. Compared to older designs, the team recorded a roughly 56,000-fold improvement in electron mobility and a maximum continuous operation of nine hours during testing.
“This study represents the first successful integration of perovskite into a betavoltaic cell, pioneering perovskite betavoltaic cells,” the researchers stated.
Betavoltaic cells work by turning beta particles—emitted during radioactive decay—into electricity. Since beta rays can’t penetrate human skin and can be blocked by materials like aluminum, the technology is considered biologically safe. Professor In explained, “I decided to use a radioactive isotope of carbon because it generates only beta rays.” Carbon-14 is also a by-product from nuclear reactors, making it cheap, widely available, and recyclable. Because it breaks down very slowly, it could power devices for hundreds or even thousands of years.
To raise energy conversion efficiency—the measure of how well a battery turns electrons into usable power—the team turned to a titanium dioxide semiconductor, often found in solar cells, and enhanced it with a ruthenium-based dye. The bond between the dye and titanium dioxide was made stronger through a citric acid treatment. When beta rays from radiocarbon hit the dye, they triggered a chain of electron reactions known as an avalanche. These electrons were then captured by the titanium dioxide and sent through a circuit to generate electric current.
The battery was also designed with radiocarbon in both the anode and cathode, increasing the amount of beta radiation and reducing energy loss over distance. This approach helped boost its energy conversion efficiency from 0.48% in older models to 2.86%.
Still, the system only converts a small portion of radioactive energy into electricity, meaning its output remains lower than standard lithium-ion batteries. Professor In suggests improving the shape of the beta emitter and finding better absorbers could further raise power output.
“This research marks the world’s first demonstration of the practical viability of betavoltaic cells,” said In. “We plan to accelerate commercialization of next-generation power supply technologies for extreme environments and pursue further miniaturization and technology transfer.”
Doctoral student Junho Lee added, “Although this research involves daily challenges that often seem impossible, we are driven by a strong sense of mission, knowing that the future of our nation is closely tied to energy security.”
The team believes that, with further development, these radiocarbon-powered batteries could be used in areas ranging from pacemakers to space probes and drones. As In puts it, “We can put safe nuclear energy into devices the size of a finger.”

• [潜在应用的乐观态度] giantg2 认为该技术可能在生物医学领域有应用，但因其低功率和放射性，在消费市场中应用有限。habibur 也指出该电池只能提供毫瓦级电力，支持的设备有限。
• [未来应用的积极展望] OneFriend2575 对新技术在传感器、医疗植入物和太空设备等领域的潜力持乐观态度，认为如果效率提升，可能会改变我们对电力的认知。
• [具体技术问题] sevensor 和其他用户如 voidUpdate 对电池的工作原理及最大电压、电流等技术细节表示关注，显示出对技术实现的兴趣。
• [关于可充电性的误解] nlitsme 指出核电池无法“充电”，纠正了有关该技术的一些误解。
• [市场化质疑] adhamsalama 对新技术能否最终进入市场表示怀疑，认为类似突破新闻往往没有下文。

补充讨论：
• [幽默/夸张的评论] pixelpoet 和 gglanzani 以幽默的方式评论，前者提到融合反应堆，后者提到运行Microsoft Teams，暗示对高能耗应用的调侃。
• [技术进步的展望] willvarfar 提出未来嵌入式纳米电子设备的广泛应用场景，例如农业中的传感器，显示出对未来技术应用的积极展望。
• [标题遗漏的关键信息] gagan2020 指出标题未提到该技术可能为小型设备供电数十年的潜力，暗示对原文报道的不满。

争议焦点：
• 新技术的实际可行性与应用前景：是否能在短期内实现量产并广泛应用，还是仅仅停留在理论或实验室阶段。
• 技术细节的透明性与可实现性：如电池的具体电压、电流及工作原理等是否能满足实际应用需求。
• 市场化与消费者接受度：是否会因为安全性、成本及效率问题无法进入市场，或仅限于某些特殊应用。

Original product description
from 2003
:
Your desktop becomes a virtual dance floor as amazingly lifelike, 3-D figures dance to the beat of your favorite tunes. Choose from a variety of dancers and dance styles, including hip-hop, disco, salsa, and more.
Get to know Amanda, Cobey, and all the other Plus! dancers by reading their bios online, and then download more of your favorite dancers to your computer.
MacPlusDancer is a delightfully nostalgic macOS app that brings back the dancers from Microsoft Plus! (their exclamation point, not mine).
Choose from a variety of dancers with different styles
Drag and position dancers anywhere on your screen
Dancers stay on top of other windows for maximum visibility
Toggle dancing on and off (except for Seth, he must dance forever)
Installation and Usage
Download the latest release from the
Releases
page.
Select a dancer from the menu bar icon (a dancing figure).
Position your dancer by dragging them around the screen.
Contributing
Contributions are welcome! Please feel free to submit a Pull Request.
NOTE: If you submit a PR to make Seth stop dancing, it will be rejected.
Legal Note
The dancer animations are from the original Microsoft Plus 2003 application. This project is not affiliated with or endorsed by Microsoft. It's a fan-made port created for educational and nostalgic purposes.

This website
from the early 2000s was very useful in building this app. Shoutout to whoever made that website, I suppose.

You should not.

We cannot legally answer that.
Q: Why is this app so big?
This app is 52 video files in a trench coat.

Yes.

data.title: GPUHammer: Rowhammer attacks on GPU memories are practical
data.author: jonbaer
data.article_summary:
**GPUHammer: Rowhammer Attacks on GPU Memories are Practical**

本文介绍了一种名为GPUHammer的攻击方法，首次展示了在GPU内存（具体为NVIDIA A6000 GPU的GDDR6内存）上实施Rowhammer比特翻转攻击的可行性。尽管GDDR6内存具有更高的延迟和更快的刷新速度，且内存映射不透明，GPUHammer仍通过逆向工程DRAM地址映射和利用GPU的SIMT并行性，成功实现了跨所有测试DRAM bank的比特翻转。攻击者可利用这些翻转篡改共享GPU环境中其他用户的数据。实验显示，单个比特翻转可使DNN模型准确率从80%降至0.1%。尽管ECC可缓解此风险，但会造成ML推理工作负载最高10%的性能下降。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：针对硬件漏洞（如锤击攻击）及其影响的技术讨论

不同观点：
• PeterStuer认为锤击攻击（hammering attacks）非常令人满意，因为它通过操作虚拟宇宙中的模式，直接影响了底层的物理层面，而不是通过传统意义上的漏洞突破。他还提出这种攻击方式让人联想到是否存在对我们现实宇宙的类似操作。
• Userbinator指出，过去GPU仅用于图形渲染时，偶尔的VRAM比特翻转并不受关注。他还提到ECC（错误校正码）在某些情况下会影响性能，尤其是当存在需要纠正的错误时。此外，他提到使用比特翻转来破坏深度神经网络（DNN）模型的概念验证，具有一定的讽刺意味，因为这些模型原本是用来模拟有错误和不精确的现实。
• Privatelypublic质疑是否存在大量分割GPU计算工作负载的情况，并询问是否有实际的例子，因为他能想到的多数情况都是使用专用GPU。
• Perching_aix作为一个硬件新手，好奇这样一个问题是如何在开发过程中的电磁模拟中被遗漏的，并提到尽管现代芯片非常复杂，难以进行完全的形式验证，但内存模块因其高度结构化的特点，可能有机会通过验证。
• IFire直接询问自己的Nvidia RTX 4090显卡上的ECC模式是否能防止这种攻击。
• Sylware提到，优化过的汇编代码相较于编译器生成的代码，可能更容易引发“锤击”问题，因为优化的代码可能更频繁地操作内存。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是ECC对性能的影响，以及在不同硬件（GPU与CPU）上的表现差异。
• 另一个讨论点是锤击攻击的实际应用场景和普遍性，尤其是对共享GPU计算资源的质疑。
• 还有人关注硬件漏洞在开发和验证过程中的检测问题，以及个人硬件（如iFire的4090显卡）如何防御此类攻击。
• 最后，讨论涉及了代码优化与硬件漏洞之间的关系，特别是汇编代码可能带来的风险。
